items.summary: SpaceX reported soaring capital expenditures on AI in its first earnings report after IPO, alongside a significant increase in revenue.

items.title: OpenAI's Computer History turns your clicks and keystrokes into a searchable ChatGPT memory timeline
items.summary: OpenAI's Computer History feature for Mac creates a searchable memory timeline for ChatGPT by recording user clicks, keystrokes, and app switches.

items.title: ChatGPT's new Computer History tracks your Mac activity to create a timeline -  but should you let it?
items.summary: ChatGPT's new Computer History feature for its Mac app tracks user activity across applications and websites to generate a timeline, raising questions about privacy.

items.title: Show HN: RAGless – similar to RAG, but $0 LLM API costs at runtime
items.summary: RAGless is presented as an alternative to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that aims to reduce LLM API costs at runtime.

items.title: MindMemOS: A Portable and Self-Evolving Memory Operating Layer for AI Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces MindMemOS, a portable and self-evolving memory operating layer designed for AI agents to enhance their ability to accumulate experience and adapt over long-term interactions.

items.title: Governed Persistent Memory: Source-Bound State Semantics and Fail-Closed Release for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Introduces Governed Persistent Memory (GPM), an auditable bitemporal state-transition model designed to manage long-term agent memory, addressing issues like contradictory or stale records. It aims to improve reliability and auditability of information stored for long-horizon AI agents.

items.title: $\varepsilon$-MemEvo: Adaptive Cross-Task Memory Transfer for LLM Program Evolution
items.summary: Introduces ε-MemEvo, a framework enabling adaptive cross-task memory transfer for LLM program evolution systems like FunSearch, preventing the discarding of search experience after task completion. This improves knowledge retention and reuse across different programming tasks.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving RAG by Concealing Sensitive Information from External LLMs
items.summary: Proposes a method for privacy-preserving Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by focusing on concealing sensitive information from external Large Language Models (LLMs). This addresses a critical privacy concern often overlooked in RAG systems.

items.title: Spatial Memory Agent: Experience-Grounded Procedure Memory for Spatial Intelligence
items.summary: Introduces a Spatial Memory Agent that leverages experience-grounded procedure memory to enhance spatial intelligence in embodied agents, robotic planning, and multimodal assistants. It aims to improve spatial reasoning abilities in VLM agents.

items.title: MARCH: Scaling Recurrent Memory with Content-Routed State Anchors
items.summary: Proposes MARCH, a method to scale recurrent memory by using content-routed state anchors, addressing the quadratic computation and linear cache growth of token-level memory.

items.title: Thought-Aware KV Cache Compaction for Reasoning via Adaptive Attention Matching
items.summary: This paper introduces a 'thought-aware KV cache compaction' method that uses adaptive attention matching to address memory bottlenecks caused by lengthy chain-of-thought sequences in reasoning language models.

items.title: HC-RAG: Evidence-Centric Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Heterogeneous Financial Filings
items.summary: This paper introduces HC-RAG (Evidence-Centric Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a system designed for financial question answering that retrieves and synthesizes information from heterogeneous financial filings.

items.title: SDAM: Structure-Difference-Aware Memory Evolution for Complex Text-to-SQL
items.summary: This paper introduces SDAM, a memory evolution framework designed for complex text-to-SQL tasks. It addresses limitations in existing memory designs, such as neglecting historical experience and weak structure analysis, to improve SQL generation.

items.title: LLMs Are Not Good Strategists, Yet Memory-Enhanced Agency Boosts Reasoning
items.summary: This research finds that while Large Language Models struggle with strategic reasoning in long-horizon environments, integrating memory-enhanced agency significantly boosts their reasoning capabilities. This memory integration helps overcome limitations like inconsistent subgoals and strategic drift.

items.title: ERSkill: Evolving for Skill-Guided Adaptive Memory Retrieval
items.summary: This research introduces ERSkill, a framework for evolving skill-guided adaptive memory retrieval in Large Language Model agents. It addresses the static nature of current memory retrieval mechanisms by making them evolvable, thereby improving performance on diverse memory queries.

items.title: When Your Agent Opens the Chat App: Agent-Controlled Search over Raw Chat Logs Rivals Structured Memory
items.summary: This research investigates whether agent-controlled search over raw chat logs can rival structured memory systems for retrieval quality, questioning how much of the benefit of structured memory comes from the structure itself.

items.title: LycheeMemory V2: Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents via Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation
items.summary: LycheeMemory V2 proposes an efficient long-term memory system for LLM agents, utilizing semantic segment-level consolidation to reduce the cost of memory construction compared to eager consolidation methods.

items.title: EgoCITE: Context-Augmented Indexing and Time-Aware Retrieval for Long-Horizon Egocentric Memory
items.summary: This paper introduces EgoCITE, a system that uses context-augmented indexing and time-aware retrieval to improve long-horizon egocentric memory, addressing bottlenecks in existing systems that transform continuous first-person video and audio into searchable records.

items.title: Features that current AIs don't have that future AIs will have
items.summary: This article speculates on future AI capabilities, highlighting features like autonomous weight updating during deployment, continual learning, and adaptively updated long-term memory, contrasting them with current AI systems.

items.title: DeepJudge unveils AI continuity protocol backed by Harvey and Thomson Reuters - globallegalpost.com
items.summary: DeepJudge has unveiled an AI continuity protocol, backed by Harvey and Thomson Reuters, which likely focuses on maintaining persistent knowledge and state for AI systems.

items.title: What we're learning about AI memory (and why most of it doesn't work yet)
items.summary: The article discusses current knowledge and challenges regarding AI memory systems, exploring why many existing approaches are not yet fully effective.

items.title: Harnessing agent memory to build lifelong AI partners for materials scientists
items.summary: This research focuses on harnessing agent memory to create lifelong AI partners for materials scientists, facilitating the accumulation and transfer of research experience and knowledge.

items.title: EvoGraph-Mem: Failure-Aware Editable Graph Memory for Long-Term Language Agents
items.summary: EvoGraph-Mem is introduced as a failure-aware editable graph memory system designed to provide long-term memory for language agents and address memory degradation.

items.title: Consolidator: Learning Persistent Routed Memory Across Context Boundaries
items.summary: This research introduces "Consolidator," a mechanism for learning persistent routed memory across context boundaries within a Phasor Memory Network. It focuses on ensuring that retained state influences subsequent memory access, not just its persistence.

items.title: Lost in Compaction: Evaluating Side-Constraint Loss under Context Compaction
items.summary: This research investigates the impact of context compaction on user-issued "Session Constraints" in LLM systems, which occurs when the context window is under pressure. It evaluates how these constraints are lost or maintained during context summarization.

items.title: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning
items.summary: This research investigates the persistence of "unlearned" knowledge in large language models by forecasting the recovery of latent traces of information. It aims to understand if residual signals of unlearned data remain detectable.

items.title: Total Recall at What Cost? Benchmarking the Serving Cost of Agentic Memory Systems
items.summary: This paper benchmarks the serving cost of agentic memory systems, comparing solutions like Mem0, Hindsight, and Mastra Observational Memory. It analyzes the economic implications of using these systems for long-running conversational agents to manage context.

items.title: LODESTAR: Trustworthy Entropy Is Navigated, Not Merely Measured -- Reinforced Polarizer Keeps a Frozen LLM from Being Confidently Misled by the Wrong Evidence
items.summary: This research proposes using predictive-distribution entropy as a selection rule in retrieval-augmented question answering (RAG) to improve trustworthiness. It shows that keeping candidate answers with the lowest answer-token entropy lifts mean answer F1 scores across five QA benchmarks.

items.title: QV-PIC: Query-Aware Visual Position-Independent Caching for Efficient RAG Serving
items.summary: This paper introduces QV-PIC, a query-aware visual position-independent caching method to enhance the efficiency of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) serving. It aims to mitigate redundant computations caused by RAG repeatedly prefilling identical text chunks across queries.

items.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges
items.summary: This research introduces SAG (SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation), a new method that enhances RAG by incorporating SQL and query-time dynamic hyperedges for LLMs. It aims to improve handling of structured constraints and multi-hop reasoning, addressing limitations in mainstream dense-retrieval RAG implementations.

items.title: Edited Is Bringing The World’s Largest Retail Dataset To AI Workspaces - WWD
items.summary: Edited is making the world's largest retail dataset available to AI workspaces, providing a vast resource for AI systems to process and utilize information.

items.title: Introducing OlmoEarth embeddings: Custom embedding exports from OlmoEarth Studio for downstream analysis
items.summary: OlmoEarth is introducing new custom embedding exports from its Studio platform, designed for downstream analysis.

items.title: TRACE: Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Conversational Engine
items.summary: This research introduces TRACE, a Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Conversational Engine designed for public service chatbots to provide reliable recommendations from noisy directories while respecting user constraints.

items.title: From Faulty Memories to Corrected Actions: Dependency-Guided Rollback Repair for Memory-Augmented Agents
items.summary: This paper proposes a dependency-guided rollback repair method to correct errors in persistent memory used by language-model agents. It addresses how faulty, stale, or misattributed memory records can alter agent reasoning and actions.

items.title: Self-Correcting Long-Horizon Search Agents via Tree-Structured Memory
items.summary: This research introduces self-correcting long-horizon search agents that utilize tree-structured memory. This method addresses unbounded context growth and noise in LLM execution trajectories by providing a structured memory mechanism.

items.title: DriveVLA-M0: Failure-Aware Memory Augmentation for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper introduces DriveVLA-M0, a failure-aware memory augmentation method for Vision-Language-Action models in autonomous driving, designed to help systems learn from past failures and adapt to distribution shifts.

items.title: Dynamic Context Adapters: Efficiently Infusing History into Vision-and-Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes Dynamic Context Adapters, a method for efficiently infusing historical context into Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to improve their performance in sequential decision-making tasks requiring temporal understanding.

items.title: Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents
items.summary: This research investigates controlled memory interference in continual large language model agents, studying how new experiences reinforce, revise, or interfere with existing long-term memory states to enable personalized behavior and evolution.

items.title: KGCache: Amortized Subgraph Retrieval for KG Reasoning with LLMs
items.summary: This work presents KGCache, a method for amortized subgraph retrieval for knowledge graph reasoning with LLMs. KGCache aims to optimize the repeated querying of graph neighborhoods that occurs when LLMs are grounded with knowledge graphs for knowledge-intensive questions.

items.title: VDGR-RAG: Vectors, Directories, Graphs, and Reflection Are All You Need for Unified Reasoning over Hierarchical Enterprise Knowledge
items.summary: This paper introduces VDGR-RAG, a system that unifies vectors, directories, graphs, and reflection for enhanced reasoning over hierarchical enterprise knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). It aims to integrate diverse retrieval strengths for better question answering in complex domains.

items.title: SodaMem: Evidence-Grounded Temporal Graph Memory for LLM Agents
items.summary: SodaMem introduces an evidence-grounded temporal graph memory system designed for LLM agents to improve long-term recall and temporal reasoning in conversations. It moves beyond traditional RAG methods to better track currency and provenance of information.

items.title: CommitKV: Lifecycle-Aware KV Cache Compression via Commit Transitions for Multi-Turn Agents
items.summary: CommitKV introduces a lifecycle-aware KV Cache compression method via commit transitions for multi-turn agents. It aims to reduce memory use and attention costs associated with growing KV caches in Reasoning-and-Acting (ReAct) agent trajectories.

items.title: SPECTRA: Pushing the KV Cache Beyond the 2-Bit Cliff via Spectral Transform Coding
items.summary: Introduces SPECTRA, a method using spectral transform coding to extend the efficiency of the KV cache in Large Language Models (LLMs) for handling longer input sequences during inference.

items.title: SAGE: SLO-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Production RAG Systems
items.summary: SAGE is an adaptive retrieval system for production Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems that dynamically adjusts retrieval budgets based on query difficulty, optimizing for service level objectives like latency and cost.

items.title: Tevatron-Elastic: A Unified Abstraction for Training Elastic Retrievers and Rerankers
items.summary: This paper presents Tevatron-Elastic, a unified abstraction for training elastic retrievers and rerankers, which are critical components for efficient information retrieval systems in AI.

items.title: Keep It Simple: Multi-Key Episodic Memory Retrieval for Ultra-Long Video Understanding
items.summary: This research proposes a multi-key episodic memory retrieval method for Multi-modal Large Language Models to enable efficient understanding of ultra-long videos by improving memory construction and retrieval.

items.title: OnEvoMemory: Evolving Memory through Online Robot Rollouts for Pretrained Robot Policies
items.summary: OnEvoMemory proposes an evolving memory module for pretrained robot policies, using online robot rollouts. This value-guided memory aims to enable long-horizon robot manipulation by tracking subtasks and interaction events.

items.title: How should we evaluate memory for AI agents?
items.summary: The article discusses methods and considerations for evaluating the memory capabilities of artificial intelligence agents.

items.title: MemOPD: On-Policy Distillation through Memory State Alignment for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: MemOPD proposes an on-policy distillation method that uses memory state alignment to create compact memory, addressing the issue of growing contexts in long-horizon agents.

items.title: TA-RAG: Tone Awareness as a Design Imperative for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper proposes TA-RAG, an approach to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that incorporates 'tone awareness' as a design imperative to handle varied communication styles in retrieved documents for LLMs.

items.title: GPTKB 2.0: Browsing, Querying, and Auditing a Disambiguated LLM-Derived Knowledge Base
items.summary: GPTKB 2.0 is a large-scale disambiguated knowledge base materialized from an LLM, containing millions of triples and entities. A web demo allows for browsing, querying, and auditing this knowledge base, which aids in AI information storage and retrieval.

items.title: Does More Retrieved Evidence Help Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Diffusion Language Models?
items.summary: This research investigates whether expanding retrieved evidence in Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) benefits Diffusion Language Models (DLMs). It challenges the assumption that more retrieved evidence always improves performance for DLMs.

items.title: From Test-Time Scaling to Reusable Memory: Measuring Crystallization in Text-to-SQL
items.summary: This paper explores the concept of 'crystallization' in Text-to-SQL systems, focusing on reusable memory for retaining verified repair episodes. It examines how systems can benefit from recalling past solutions to recurring queries, rather than discarding computation.

items.title: CoinRAG: Contextualized Information Nugget KV Cache Reuse for Long-Context RAG
items.summary: CoinRAG introduces a novel optimization technique for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by utilizing contextualized information nugget KV cache reuse for long contexts. This method aims to improve RAG efficiency by reducing redundancy and noise.

items.title: AtlasVLA: Persistent World-Ego State Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: AtlasVLA introduces persistent world-ego state modeling for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, addressing the limitation of perception forgetting in embodied AI tasks, especially with single-camera setups.

items.title: LifelongCrossNav: Persistent 3D Semantic Memory for Cross-Floor Multi-Object Navigation
items.summary: LifelongCrossNav is a framework for sequential multi-object navigation in unknown environments, focusing on persistent 3D semantic memory to enable cross-floor navigation for object-goal tasks.

items.title: Lybrary,a persistent AST-aware code memory for AI agents(MCP server pip install)
items.summary: Lybrary is a persistent, Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-aware code memory system designed for AI agents, installable as an MCP server.

items.title: Tencent Cloud Open-Sources TencentDB Agent Memory v2.0: A Team-Level Memory Hub for AI Coding Agents
items.summary: Tencent Cloud has open-sourced TencentDB Agent Memory v2.0, a team-level memory hub designed for AI coding agents that transforms conversations, documents, and code into reusable memory assets.

items.title: Building a Multimodal RAG Pipeline with NVIDIA NeMo Retriever, Hosted NIMs, LanceDB, Reranking, and Grounded Generation
items.summary: This tutorial details how to construct an advanced multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline using NVIDIA NeMo Retriever, LanceDB, and reranking techniques. It focuses on how AI systems store and recall information for generation.

items.title: Show HN: Alyph, a manual transmission for LLM context
items.summary: Alyph is introduced as a tool allowing users to manually control and edit the context of LLM interactions, enabling changes to the AI's response history and branching conversations.

items.title: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
items.summary: Activity Frames is a deterministic, zero-model pipeline that compiles passively captured screen activity into agent memory, allowing computer-use agents to store and replay user routines instead of re-deriving them.

items.title: Runtime Observability for Heterogeneous Attention Memory
items.summary: This research proposes a runtime observability contract for heterogeneous attention memory in modern AI models, covering various memory types like KV cache, latent caches, and recurrent states to understand their behavior under compression.

items.title: QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding
items.summary: This paper introduces QEvict, a method for recoverable quantized Key-Value (KV) eviction designed to reduce the memory footprint of the KV cache in autoregressive large language models. It enables attention-drift-robust long-context decoding.

items.title: KV-Skill: Forging Expertise in the Model's Native Language
items.summary: This paper introduces KV-Skill, a design space for forging expertise within a model's native language by exploring alternative methods for storing task knowledge. It aims to improve modularity and shareability of model capabilities.

items.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces Align-RAG, a method for retrieval-augmented forecasting that adapts frozen Time Series Foundation Models to new domains using in-context learning. It focuses on alignment for merging retrieved examples without fine-tuning.

items.title: Universal Pathologies, Conditional Consequences: A Triple-Robustness Analysis of RAG for Multi-Hop Traceability
items.summary: This research presents a triple-robustness analysis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for multi-hop traceability. It compares GraphRAG and vector RAG performance, varying embedders and corpora to understand pathologies and consequences.

items.title: Sparse Mutual Information Graph Averaging for Improving Random Indexing Embeddings
items.summary: This paper proposes using sparse mutual information graph averaging to refine random indexing (RI) vectors, aiming to improve sparse word embeddings in AI systems.

items.title: NeSy-RAG: Neuro-Symbolic RAG for Explainable Question Answering
items.summary: Introduces NeSy-RAG, a neuro-symbolic Retrieval-Augmented Generation system designed to improve explainable question answering by grounding Large Language Models in external knowledge.

items.title: Show HN: GreatArrow.ai – Shared memory for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Cursor
items.summary: GreatArrow.ai introduces a shared memory solution designed for various large language models, including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Cursor.

items.title: User awareness in frontier models
items.summary: This article explores 'user awareness' in advanced AI models, detailing how AI assistants integrate user-specific information, such as email addresses, into their operational context.

items.title: FinPerMA: A Theory-Informed, Event-Grounded Personalized-Memory Benchmark for LLM Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces FinPerMA, a personalized-memory benchmark for LLM agents designed to evaluate their ability to maintain and update individualized user models over long interactions, particularly in high-stakes domains like financial advising.

items.title: SafeCommit: Certifying When Memory-Grounded Agents May Safely Act
items.summary: This paper introduces SafeCommit, a framework for certifying when memory-grounded agents can safely act, specifically addressing the problem of premature commitment due to stale, conflicting, or corrupted memory grounding in long-horizon agents.

items.title: Hierarchical Graph Memory for LLM Agents with Path-level Localization and Rewrite
items.summary: This research introduces hierarchical graph memory for LLM agents, designed for long-term reasoning with efficient updates, path-level localization, and rewrite capabilities. It aims to improve structural organization for multi-hop retrieval and reasoning.

items.title: RAG-Stack: Co-Optimizing RAG Serving Performance and Quality
items.summary: RAG-Stack is a system designed for co-optimizing the serving performance and quality of Retrieval-augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It addresses the complexity of configuring various components like retrieval indexes to enhance knowledge-intensive LLM applications.

items.title: D$^2$F-ReAG: Dynamic Decomposition and Filtering for Multi-Hop Reasoning-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces D$^2$F-ReAG, a method that uses dynamic decomposition and filtering to enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for multi-hop reasoning, addressing LLMs' reliance on static internal knowledge.

items.title: Relevant but Incomplete: Referential Dangling as a Paradigm-Level Failure Mode in Hard Prompt Compression
items.summary: This paper identifies 'Referential Dangling' as a structural failure in hard prompt compression techniques, where independent selection can split dependent evidence pairs, leading to incomplete context.

items.title: The Personalization Mirage: How LLMs Fabricate User Profiles, and Why Self-Monitoring Misleads
items.summary: This study examines 'over-inference' in personalized LLMs with persistent memory, where models fabricate user attributes, introducing MirageBench to evaluate this phenomenon.

items.title: When Memory Lies: An Empirical Study of Spatial Memory Staleness in VLM Agents
items.summary: This empirical study investigates 'Spatial Memory Staleness' in memory-augmented VLM agents, exploring how outdated persistent spatial knowledge affects their ability to reconcile memory claims with observations.

items.title: Caching for the Future: Scrub Jay Episodic Memory Principles for Agent Memory Systems
items.summary: This research proposes applying "Scrub Jay Episodic Memory Principles" to agent memory systems to manage the varying validity of stored memories across sessions. It aims to prevent contamination of retrieved context with outdated facts by treating memory persistence based on content type.

items.title: InsightEmb: Learning Action-Intent Embeddings for Agentic Insight Retrieval
items.summary: This paper introduces InsightEmb, a method for learning action-intent embeddings to facilitate agentic insight retrieval, allowing self-improving agents to efficiently recall reusable insights from past experiences. This improves an agent's ability to progress towards its goal by retrieving relevant information at each decision step.

items.title: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
items.summary: FocusMem proposes a method for factorizing content, readout, and trust in latent GUI memory for AI agents. It offers a compact solution for agents to remember useful experiences and unfinished progress by compressing multimodal trajectories into continuous tokens.

items.title: Explicit Language Memory for Long-Horizon Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Proposes integrating explicit language memory into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to overcome challenges in long-horizon planning and improve cross-task compositional generalization.

items.title: BridgeVLA++: A Data-Efficient, Generalizable, and Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Framework for 3D Manipulation
items.summary: Presents BridgeVLA++, a data-efficient and generalizable Vision-Language-Action framework for 3D robot manipulation, which is memory-augmented to address limitations of existing VLA methods.

items.title: Callosium, one shared memory for every AI, in plain Markdown files
items.summary: Callosium is introduced as a shared memory system for AI, storing information in plain Markdown files for persistent recall.

items.title: ISEE: Interactive Semantic Enrichment for Database Fields
items.summary: ISEE proposes an Interactive Semantic Enrichment method to improve the clarity and completeness of database field descriptions, enhancing the performance of LLM-based agents in data-related tasks like retrieval.

items.title: Verifiable Memory: Learning Unified Memory Management with Local and Global Verifiers for Large Language Model Agents
items.summary: This research introduces "Verifiable Memory," a framework for unified memory management in large language model agents using local and global verifiers. It addresses challenges in retaining information and controlling context during long-horizon interactions.

items.title: LeanMem: Simple and Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces LeanMem, a novel long-term memory system designed to be simple and efficient for LLM agents. It addresses the challenges of existing memory systems that often lead to excessive token consumption or loss of detail when processing heterogeneous dialogue content.

items.title: Output-Aware Rotation for INT2 KV-Cache Quantization
items.summary: This research proposes an output-aware rotation technique for INT2 KV-cache quantization, aiming to address the memory and bandwidth bottleneck in long-context large language model inference. It improves ultra-low-bit quantization by optimizing with consideration for the complete attention output.

items.title: Designing a Good Virtual Node: Addressable and Cardinality-Preserving Global Memory for Message Passing Architectures
items.summary: This research explores designing effective virtual nodes for message-passing neural networks to create an addressable and cardinality-preserving global memory. It aims to improve global communication routes within these architectures.

items.title: Maglev: Sliding Recurrent Memory
items.summary: This paper introduces Maglev, a recurrent Transformer architecture featuring fixed-size memory that generalizes sliding-window attention. The architecture is designed to remain parallelizable during training.

items.title: AnchorKV: Anchor-Residual KV Cache Compression
items.summary: This paper introduces AnchorKV, a method for compressing the key-value (KV) cache, which is a primary memory bottleneck in long-context LLM inference. It aims to improve efficiency by addressing the limitations of existing eviction and quantization methods.

items.title: Lightweight Chunk Selection for Mobile Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces a lightweight chunk selection method to optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for mobile and edge devices. It aims to reduce computation and memory costs by retaining only one retrieved chunk.

items.title: SAKI: Score-Aware Low-Rank Key Indexing for Long-Context KV Retrieval
items.summary: This research introduces SAKI, a Score-Aware Low-Rank Key Indexing method for long-context KV retrieval. It aims to optimize key compression by directly addressing expected attention score distortion.

items.title: PI-Mem: Pushing Long-Context Reasoning to 3.6M Tokens with Parallel-Iterative Memory
items.summary: PI-Mem is a new parallel-iterative memory approach designed to overcome long-context reasoning bottlenecks in Large Language Models (LLMs), pushing capabilities to 3.6 million tokens by addressing challenges in sequential updates and inter-chunk dependencies.

items.title: Ask HN: What is a good format for a tool to report data to a LLM?
items.summary: A discussion inquires about the most effective data format for tools to report structured or tabular information to Large Language Models (LLMs) for efficient processing.

items.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs
items.summary: French startup Kog is focusing on deeper optimization to extract more inference performance from GPUs, challenging the notion that GPUs are poorly suited for agentic workflows.

items.title: Hyperscalers might regret embracing natural gas if new forecast proves correct
items.summary: A new forecast suggests natural gas prices could triple in parts of the U.S., potentially leading to massive power bills for hyperscalers operating AI data centers.

items.title: Data center backlash echoes fossil-fuel politics
items.summary: The article highlights growing public opposition to data centers, including a protest by Willie Nelson, underscoring the political and environmental backlash against essential AI infrastructure.

items.title: Why the Infrastructure Gap Is Holding Financial AI Back and What Kaleshwar Aryasomayajula Has Been Doing to Solve It
items.summary: This article examines how the existing infrastructure gap is impeding the advancement of AI in the financial industry and highlights Kaleshwar Aryasomayajula's efforts to address this challenge.

items.title: 7 AI Coding Assistants Developers Should Try in 2026
items.summary: An article suggests seven AI coding assistants that developers should consider trying in 2026.

items.title: 4 Best Tools to Track How AI Chatbots Feel About Your Brand in 2026
items.summary: An article lists the four best tools for tracking how AI chatbots perceive or "feel" about a brand.

items.title: Show HN: Security scanner for SaaS build with AI
items.summary: A new security scanner for Software as a Service (SaaS) applications, built with AI, has been showcased.

items.title: From assistance to execution: How enterprises put AI to work
items.summary: The article discusses how enterprises are implementing and utilizing AI systems to transition from assistance to execution.

items.title: Bitcoin: 4,962 anomalies detected by a Chinese AI, alert rises - Cointribune
items.summary: A Chinese AI system detected 4,962 anomalies related to Bitcoin, raising an alert.

items.title: Ask HN: How do you use AI for learning?
items.summary: A discussion thread explores various ways individuals are using AI for learning and educational purposes.

items.title: Can an AI model’s ‘reasoning’ be extracted? New research fuels US-China distillation row - The Indian Express
items.summary: New research investigating whether an AI model's reasoning can be extracted is contributing to a geopolitical debate between the US and China over model distillation.

items.title: DeepSeek publishes paper on self-evolving AI framework Cordis - kucoin.com
items.summary: DeepSeek published a paper detailing Cordis, a self-evolving AI framework.

items.title: How AI is helping to open a new chapter for ancient Chinese literature - South China Morning Post
items.summary: AI is being utilized to analyze and interpret ancient Chinese literature, thereby opening new avenues for understanding and research in the field.

items.title: Position: Reasoning is a Learnable Rule-Based Process
items.summary: This position paper argues that autonomous reasoning in AI, a topic of significant scientific and economic interest, is best understood as a learnable rule-based process, moving from symbolic AI to deep probabilistic generative models.

items.title: Dual-Flow Transformers: Decoupling the Primary Prefill Path from Additional Decode Computation
items.summary: This paper introduces Dual-Flow Transformers, an architecture designed to decouple the prompt prefill path from decode computation in LLMs, aiming to optimize inference cost and efficiency.

items.title: Learning to Adapt Cross-Domain Preferences via Meta-LoRA for LLM Personalization
items.summary: This paper introduces Meta-LoRA, a new method that uses meta-learning to adapt large language models to cross-domain user preferences for enhanced personalization with limited data.

items.title: Large Language Models Can Follow Instructions, But Not Many at Once: Phase Transitions in Compositional Constraint Satisfaction
items.summary: This research explores the limitations of large language models in simultaneously adhering to multiple explicit constraints, observing phase transitions when numerous compositional constraints are applied.

items.title: CAS: A Causal Attribution Score for Local and Global Explainable Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: Introduces the Causal Attribution Score (CAS), a compact architecture for causal explanation in AI, designed to attribute intervention effects on real-world outcomes. This method aims to improve explainability in AI systems beyond just predictive explanations.

items.title: Trie Automata for Constrained Decoding over Large Finite Sets
items.summary: Proposes using Trie Automata as a method for constrained decoding in large language models, specifically to enable generating structured outputs that conform to predefined finite sets of valid strings. This offers an alternative to general-purpose grammar compilation for such tasks.

items.title: Dead text or binding clause? Measuring and restoring constraint influence in black-box LLM dialogues
items.summary: Investigates "behavioral relapse" or "revocation inertia" in black-box LLM dialogues, where models fail to reliably act upon withdrawn user constraints. The paper measures this phenomenon and suggests methods to restore constraint influence.

items.title: Designing AI Pipelines for Decision-Ready ITSM Intelligence
items.summary: Presents a sociotechnical AI pipeline designed and evaluated using design science research principles, aimed at transforming large volumes of heterogeneous IT service management (ITSM) ticket data into actionable intelligence for stakeholders.

items.title: On the Expressive Power of Transformers
items.summary: Investigates the expressive power of multi-layer transformers, a critical component of large language models, aiming to precisely calibrate their capabilities as language recognizers. This study delves into the fundamental theoretical properties of this architecture.

items.title: The Role of Natural Language Understanding in Multimodal Video-Based Dengue Diagnosis
items.summary: Explores the role of Natural Language Understanding in multimodal video-based dengue diagnosis, focusing on detecting infection-related behavioral changes in mosquitoes from video data despite environmental challenges.

items.title: Beyond the Best Guess: Improving LLM Solution Coverage with Evolution Strategies
items.summary: Proposes using evolution strategies to improve the solution coverage of Large Language Models in discovery domains like math and science. This goes beyond a single "best guess" to enhance the models' ability to generate diverse and effective solutions.

items.title: PROVE-RT: Generating Mechanized Theorem Prover Scripts for Real-Time Systems using LLMs
items.summary: Introduces PROVE-RT, a method for generating mechanized theorem prover scripts for real-time systems using Large Language Models, aiming to provide a more rigorous and scalable alternative to traditional pen-and-paper proofs for schedulability analysis.

items.title: Foundations of MT-PDCL: Measure-Theoretic Probabilistic Definite Clause Logic
items.summary: Introduces Measure-Theoretic Probabilistic Definite Clause Logic (MT-PDCL), a new framework addressing limitations of standard probabilistic logic programming for exact inference in finite domains.

items.title: EEG-PRIME: Prototype-Aligned Representation Learning with Multi-Level Conditioning for EEG Decoding
items.summary: Proposes EEG-PRIME, a two-stage EEG foundation model that uses prototype-aligned representation learning and multi-level conditioning for robust cross-dataset multi-task EEG decoding.

items.title: Numeracy in Large Language Models: Fundamental Limitations and Paths to Improvement
items.summary: A survey examining the fundamental limitations of Large Language Models in numerical understanding and elementary mathematical tasks, and suggesting paths for improvement.

items.title: Unifying Generative Models with Path Integrals
items.summary: This paper formulates a unified theoretical framework for generative modeling using path integrals, where various generative models arise from different evaluation principles. It describes the Martin-Siggia-Rose-Janssen-de~Dominicis form to separate free from interacting probability flow.

items.title: Dual Spatial-Temporal Attribution: Architecture-Aligned Post-Hoc Explainability for Recurrent Graph Anomaly Detection
items.summary: This research addresses the opacity of deep learning detectors for anomalies in dynamic graphs by proposing a dual spatial-temporal attribution method for post-hoc explainability. The goal is to provide reasons for flagged anomalies, which is crucial for deployment in regulated information systems.

items.title: Geometric and Behavioral Stratification in Transformer Residual Streams
items.summary: This paper investigates the internal workings of trained transformer models, focusing on "privileged bases" within residual streams. It explores the prediction and unembedding directions to understand how these coordinate axes influence model behavior.

items.title: Learning Under Treatment-Induced Label Indeterminacy with Expert Annotations of Counterfactual Outcomes: A Case Study in Neurological Prognostication
items.summary: This study addresses the challenge of label indeterminacy in clinical prediction models, particularly when treatment decisions make outcomes unobservable, using a case study in neurological prognostication. It proposes using expert annotations of counterfactual outcomes for learning in such scenarios.

items.title: Exploring Oversmoothing with Householder Matrices
items.summary: This research explores the phenomenon of oversmoothing in deep graph neural networks (GNNs), where node representations collapse with increasing network depth. It proposes using Householder matrices to study and address this issue.

items.title: GENADA: efficient generative time series adversarial attack framework
items.summary: This paper introduces GENADA, an efficient generative time series adversarial attack framework, to expose the vulnerability of deep learning models used in time series analysis. It demonstrates how small input perturbations can severely degrade predictive performance.

items.title: Prof-K: Probabilistic One-Pass Filtering for Efficient Top-k Selection
items.summary: This paper introduces Prof-K, a probabilistic one-pass filtering method designed for efficient top-k selection, a fundamental computational primitive. It aims to address the inefficiency of existing approaches for large data sizes in various machine learning workloads.

items.title: Represent, Then Generate: Multimodal-Conditioned Time-Series Generation under Irregular Missingness
items.summary: This research proposes a method for multimodal-conditioned time-series generation to synthesize absent physiological signals from co-recorded data, addressing irregular missingness in clinical monitoring. The approach aims to provide a remedy when informative signals are unavailable.

items.title: Predicting When Random Low-Dimensional Reparameterizations Train Neural Networks
items.summary: This paper investigates the conditions under which neural networks can be effectively trained or fine-tuned using random low-dimensional reparameterization. It explores the necessary size of the latent search space to reach a low-loss region.

items.title: Structure-preserving uncertainty quantification for GENERIC dynamics
items.summary: This research focuses on developing methods for structure-preserving uncertainty quantification (UQ) for machine learning models that embed physical structures directly into their architectures. It addresses limitations where standard UQ methods may violate encoded admissibility conditions.

items.title: Interpretable Causal Discovery via Causal-Effect Constraints
items.summary: This research proposes a method for interpretable causal discovery by using causal-effect constraints to uncover underlying causal relationships from data. The goal is to not only predict causal edges but also to explain observed or hypothesized phenomena.

items.title: Training Under Challenge: Executable Certificates and Challenge-Closed Optimality for Neural Networks
items.summary: This paper introduces "Training Under Challenge," an executable-certificate framework designed to provide deeper insights into the training process and optimality of neural networks. It aims to reveal whether a network has reached a global optimum or is limited in other ways, beyond what a flat training curve indicates.

items.title: Finding the Needle in a Haystack: Test-Time Analog Circuit Representation Adaptation for Bayesian Optimization
items.summary: This research proposes a test-time analog circuit representation adaptation method for Bayesian optimization (BO) to efficiently search for analog circuit topologies. It addresses the mismatch caused by fixed circuit embeddings after encoder training.

items.title: The Impact of Temporal Context Length and Encoding Strategies on Self-Supervised ECG Representation Learning
items.summary: This research investigates the impact of temporal context length and encoding strategies on self-supervised electrocardiogram (ECG) representation learning. It explores how these choices affect information needed for rhythm inference and longitudinal consistency in real-world recordings.

items.title: A Contract-Grade Verifier for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels, and a Native Blackwell Backward for the Gated-Linear-Recurrence Family
items.summary: This paper presents a "Contract-Grade Verifier" for GPU kernels generated by Large Language Models, aiming to ensure higher correctness beyond simple random input tests. It also introduces a native Blackwell Backward for the Gated-Linear-Recurrence family.

items.title: Federated Compositional Muon Optimizer for Matrix-Wise Models
items.summary: This paper proposes a Federated Compositional Muon Optimizer designed to improve the performance of Muon, a recently developed optimizer, for matrix-wise models in AI, particularly for hierarchical structured problems.

items.title: Perturbation-based Regional Interpretability through Subtraction Mapping (PRISM): naming-error dissociations in language models and post-stroke aphasia
items.summary: This research introduces PRISM (Perturbation-based Regional Interpretability through Subtraction Mapping), a new method for mechanistic interpretability of large language models. It adapts subtraction analysis from human neuroimaging to test for specialized internal components in language models.

items.title: A Cloud-Edge System for Multimodal Clinical Screening in Resource-Constrained Rural Settings
items.summary: This research proposes a cloud-edge system for multimodal clinical screening, designed to make medical AI diagnostic capabilities accessible in resource-constrained rural settings with limited bandwidth and compute.

items.title: Decentralized Multi-Player Q-Learning in Episodic Markov Decision Processes with Information Asymmetry
items.summary: This study investigates decentralized multi-player reinforcement learning using Q-learning in episodic Markov Decision Processes, specifically examining how different forms of information asymmetry impact the learning process.

items.title: A Compositional Theory of Curvature in Probabilistic Circuits
items.summary: This paper develops a compositional theory of curvature for Probabilistic Circuits, which are generative models that support exact inference, focusing on their loss-surface curvature.

items.title: Robust data-driven discovery of fractional differential equations via weak formulations and Pareto-based subset selection
items.summary: This research proposes a robust data-driven method, called Weak-Pareto, for discovering fractional differential equations from noisy data by combining weak formulations and Pareto-based subset selection.

items.title: EGRL: Edge generation-guided relation-aware learning for RNA-protein interaction prediction
items.summary: This paper introduces EGRL, an edge generation-guided relation-aware learning method using Graph Neural Networks for efficiently predicting RNA-Protein Interactions, which are critical for cellular functions.

items.title: Revisiting Overestimation Bias Problem of Q-learning: Settling Large Discrete Action Space via Action Intersection
items.summary: This paper re-examines the overestimation bias problem in Q-learning, particularly in settings with large discrete action spaces, proposing an action intersection method to mitigate the issue.

items.title: Towards Socially Compliant Navigation in Deep Reinforcement Learning via Proxemics-Based Reward Modeling
items.summary: This research proposes a proxemics-based reward modeling approach for deep reinforcement learning to enable socially compliant robot navigation in crowded environments.

items.title: Momentum as Residual-Driven Multiplier Correction for Deep Learning Optimization
items.summary: This paper introduces an ADMM-Inspired Momentum (AIM) framework to better understand and improve momentum-based optimizers in deep learning by treating momentum as a residual-driven multiplier correction.

items.title: Multi-perspective Imbalance-Conscious 6G Beamforming Optimization and Performance
items.summary: This study applies machine learning to optimize 6G-IoT beamforming, comparing supervised and unsupervised approaches and evaluating various feature groups for performance.

items.title: Understanding Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Vertical Federated Learning: The Gap Between Research and Practice
items.summary: This paper examines backdoor vulnerabilities within Vertical Federated Learning, analyzing the gap between current research and practical implications for model training and privacy.

items.title: Comment on "Modeling rapid language learning by distilling Bayesian priors into artificial neural networks"
items.summary: This paper comments on a previous work, discussing the proposal that Artificial Neural Networks can learn formal languages by distilling Bayesian priors into them via Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning.

items.title: Learning the Mathematical Property for Designing Low Mutual Coherence Binary Sensing Matrices
items.summary: This research focuses on using a learning-based technique to discover the mathematical properties required for designing low mutual coherence binary sensing matrices, essential for compressive sensing.

items.title: On the global feature importance for interpretable and trustworthy heat demand forecasting
items.summary: This paper introduces an ante-hoc Explainable AI methodology to assess global feature importance in Machine Learning models for heat demand forecasting, aiming to enhance their interpretability and trustworthiness in intelligent control systems.

items.title: Learning Discrete Decisions for MIPs with Constraint-Aware Diffusion
items.summary: This paper proposes a novel learning-based approach utilizing constraint-aware diffusion to approximately solve computationally challenging mixed-integer optimization problems.

items.title: Sampling Luck Masquerades as Allocation Gain: Auditing Test-Time Budget Allocation for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
items.summary: This research audits the impact of test-time budget allocation strategies for Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO) solvers, revealing how sampling variability can masquerade as allocation gains.

items.title: FlowLOB: Efficient and Controllable Limit Order Book Generation with Flow Matching
items.summary: This paper introduces FlowLOB, a new method using flow matching for efficient, controllable, and realistic generation of limit order book (LOB) dynamics for market simulators.

items.title: LLMs Know the Constraint But Do Not Use It: Activation Bottlenecks in Pragmatic Constraint Reasoning
items.summary: This paper investigates why Large Language Models (LLMs) often fail to use internally encoded constraints in pragmatic reasoning, formalizing the concept of conditional constraint activation.

items.title: What Drives LLM Self-Reflection? A Controlled Ablation of Uncertainty Routing in Armed Conflict Forecasting
items.summary: This research presents a controlled ablation study to understand which components, such as evidence exposure and diagnostic scaffolding, drive improvements in LLM self-reflection for reasoning tasks.

items.title: On Measuring Semantic Preservation in Legal Ontology Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of measuring semantic preservation in legal ontology learning, highlighting limitations in current evaluation methodologies that focus on structural correctness rather than meaning.

items.title: LoRA-Diffusion: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Low-Rank Trajectory Decomposition
items.summary: This paper introduces LoRA-Diffusion, a novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that extends low-rank adaptation techniques to diffusion-based language models.

items.title: Reliability-Aware Sexism Detection: Combining DPO with Annotator Agreement and Token-Level Confidence Scoring
items.summary: This research proposes a reliability-aware method for sexism detection, combining DPO with annotator agreement and token-level confidence scoring to address the inherent subjectivity of the task.

items.title: Can Spectral-Clipping Enable Better Learning While Forgetting Less for Low-Rank Adaptation?
items.summary: This work explores whether spectral-clipping can enhance low-rank adaptation (LoRA) by enabling better learning while reducing catastrophic forgetting in neural network fine-tuning.

items.title: Steering the Language Axis: From Linear Decodability to Causal Control
items.summary: This research investigates the latent dynamics of language selection in Large Language Models, exploring whether language identity can be causally controlled by compact activation mechanisms.

items.title: StorySpark: Module-wise Evolutionary Search for Story Premise Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces StorySpark, a new system that employs a module-wise evolutionary search for generating diverse and creative story premises using LLM-based approaches.

items.title: From Refuse to Richness: Rubric Rewards for Long-Form Hallucination Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This research investigates using rubric rewards in reinforcement learning to improve grounding and reduce long-form hallucination in generative models, analyzing the trade-off between refusal and richness.

items.title: Predicting consumer-technology ownership without a diffusion history
items.summary: This study investigates whether the perceived attributes of consumer technology can predict ownership without historical diffusion data. It utilizes both human survey responses and ratings from frontier language models, including Anthropic Claude Opus, to analyze this predictive capability.

items.title: New Terms, New Toxicity: Consensus-based Chinese Neologism Toxicity Detection via Search-Augmented LLMs
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for consensus-based Chinese neologism toxicity detection using search-augmented Large Language Models. It addresses the challenge of identifying evolving toxic expressions in new terms that pose difficulties for traditional moderation systems.

items.title: Are you Talking Logic to Me? Assessing Language Models Syllogistic Reasoning Capabilities
items.summary: This research assesses the syllogistic reasoning capabilities of language models, which often struggle with logical tasks. It investigates how different formal Knowledge Representation notations impact models' ability to solve these reasoning challenges.

items.title: Query Timing Produces Opposite Positional Biases Between LLMs and Humans
items.summary: This study examines positional biases, such as recency and primacy effects, in Large Language Models compared to humans, specifically investigating how query timing can produce opposite biases. It aims to understand the underlying mechanisms of these evaluation biases in LLMs.

items.title: DIVE: Unlocking Self-Improvement in Frozen Language Models Through Diversity-Driven Skill Evolution
items.summary: This research introduces DIVE, a diversity-driven framework enabling "frozen" Large Language Models to achieve self-improvement. DIVE allows LLMs to evolve persistent natural-language skills from task experience and verifier feedback without requiring parameter updates.

items.title: Novels generated by language models show compressed formal variation
items.summary: This study analyzes novels generated by Large Language Models, finding that their output shows compressed formal variation across multiple generations. It investigates the stylistic diversity of AI-generated long-form content, rather than focusing on individual passage detection.

items.title: PatientAct: Theory-Grounded Mental Health Client Simulation
items.summary: This paper introduces PatientAct, a theory-grounded mental health client simulation system utilizing LLMs. It aims to create more realistic simulated clients for training novice counselors and evaluating LLM therapists, addressing limitations of overly cooperative existing simulators.

items.title: ViTOED: A Dataset for Target-Oriented Emotion Detection on Vietnamese Social Media Texts
items.summary: This paper introduces ViTOED, a novel dataset for target-oriented emotion detection in Vietnamese social media texts, comprising over 10,000 user comments and 21,000 manually annotated opinion quadruples. This dataset aims to support research in natural language processing for low-resource languages.

items.title: CRAFT: LLM-Based Iterative Refinement for Temporal Reasoning over Clinical Narratives
items.summary: This paper introduces CRAFT, an LLM-based iterative refinement framework for temporal reasoning over clinical narratives. CRAFT aims to understand the temporal progression of symptoms from clinical texts, which is crucial for disease monitoring and safety surveillance.

items.title: From Atomic Evidence to Logical Composition: Structured Compositional Reasoning over Compound Answer Options
items.summary: This research introduces a framework to improve large language models' ability to perform structured compositional reasoning over compound answer options involving logical operators like AND, OR, and NEITHER/NOR. It addresses LLM failures when combining atomic judgments correctly.

items.title: Falsehood and Impossibility Are Different Directions in an AI's Representation of Language
items.summary: This paper reports an exploratory activation study on the multimodal open-weight model Gemma 3 4B IT, investigating whether AI models internally distinguish between false and impossible linguistic statements.

items.title: Prompts in the Wild: A Large Analyzed Collection of Transactional Prompts in Code
items.summary: This paper presents a large analyzed collection of transactional prompts found in code, arguing that prompts for generative Large Language Models are linguistic objects deserving of investigation.

items.title: HybridRAG-BN: A Retrieval-Augmented Framework with Fine-Tuned Verification for Bangla KBQA
items.summary: HybridRAG-BN is a new retrieval-augmented framework with fine-tuned verification designed for Knowledge-Base Question Answering (KBQA) in Bangla, aiming to address challenges in low-resource languages.

items.title: Better Decomposition, Free Aggregation: A Synthesizer-Folding Framework for Multilingual Multi-Hop Question Answering
items.summary: This paper introduces a Synthesizer-Folding Framework for Multilingual Multi-Hop Question Answering, designed to improve multilingual retrieval-augmented generation by enabling large language models to access globally distributed external knowledge.

items.title: Localize, Then Reason: Visual Latent Structural Reasoning for Molecular Properties and Edits
items.summary: This research proposes a method for visual latent structural reasoning for molecular properties and edits, improving LLM-based chemical reasoning by combining local chemical perception with property reasoning from molecular images.

items.title: Self-Referential Induction Increases Response Instability Relative to Unresolvable and Verifiable Questions in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates how self-referential induction affects the response instability of large language models compared to unresolvable and verifiable questions, measuring the consistency of reports resembling subjective experience.

items.title: Surface-to-Skeleton 3D Cephalometry: Estimating Hidden Skeletal Landmarks from CT-Derived External Soft-Tissue Surfaces
items.summary: This research proposes a method for 3D cephalometry to estimate hidden internal skeletal landmarks from external soft-tissue surfaces derived from CT scans, addressing limitations of existing facial-landmark methods.

items.title: Attribute-Conditioned Multimodal Slot Factorization for Controllable Fashion Retrieval
items.summary: This paper proposes Attribute-Conditioned Multimodal Slot Factorization, a new method for controllable fashion retrieval that allows satisfying multiple attributes simultaneously, unlike monolithic embeddings that hinder specific control.

items.title: PseudoMapLabeler: Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Label Generation for Semi-Supervised Online Mapping
items.summary: This paper introduces PseudoMapLabeler, a teacher-student semi-supervised learning framework that generates confidence-aware pseudo-labels for online HD map construction, addressing the challenge of scarce labeled training data in diverse environments.

items.title: Inference-Time Orthogonal Seeding Enables Geometry-Aligned 3D Organ Segmentation for Slice-Propagation Methods
items.summary: This research proposes inference-time orthogonal seeding to enable geometry-aligned 3D organ segmentation for slice-propagation methods, aiming to reduce the burden of dense voxel-level annotation in medical imaging.

items.title: A Generative Approach for Improving Multi-Label Defect Classification in Photovoltaic Modules
items.summary: This paper proposes a generative approach to improve multi-label defect classification in electroluminescence images of photovoltaic cells, addressing the learning ambiguity caused by co-occurring defects during model training.

items.title: Dual-Manifold Geometry Guided Representation Learning: Adaptive Coupling between Kernel and Data Spaces
items.summary: This paper introduces a dual-manifold perspective for deep representation learning, focusing on the structured geometry embedded in network parameters and proposing an adaptive coupling between kernel and data spaces within convolutional layers.

items.title: Dual-Stream Cross-Anchor Correction Grounding Long-Form Captions and the Domain Limits of Object-Level Anchors
items.summary: This research addresses object hallucination in multimodal large language models by proposing a Dual-Stream Cross-Anchor Correction Grounding method for long-form captions, aiming to better tie individual object mentions to visual evidence.

items.title: Scaling Representation Diversity: Modulated Attention and Reconstructive Regularization for Visual Grounding
items.summary: This work re-examines Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) from an open-vocabulary grounding perspective, proposing Modulated Attention and Reconstructive Regularization to scale representation diversity and improve cross-dataset generalization.

items.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
items.summary: This paper introduces SCOPE, a method for Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention, aiming to reduce the quadratic self-attention cost in Diffusion Transformers over spatiotemporal tokens.

items.title: Structured Local Differential Modeling for AI-Generated Image Detection
items.summary: This paper proposes Structured Local Differential Modeling for AI-Generated Image Detection, a new method to reliably detect AI-generated content by overcoming the dominance of semantically salient components in existing detection methods.

items.title: Heterogeneous Vision-Language Ensemble with Disagreement-Aware Reranking for Text-Based Person Anomaly Retrieval
items.summary: This work proposes a heterogeneous vision-language ensemble with disagreement-aware reranking to improve text-based person anomaly retrieval from large image galleries using natural language descriptions.

items.title: SPARED: Reasoning-Based AI-Generated Image Detection via Adversarially Edited Data
items.summary: This research introduces SPARED, a reasoning-based method for detecting AI-generated images that also justifies its verdicts, addressing limitations of existing detectors regarding provenance shortcuts and explanations.

items.title: NaviDC-OCR: Navigating Document Parsing Across Digital and Camera-Captured Documents
items.summary: This paper introduces NaviDC-OCR, an approach that uses Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to navigate document parsing across both digital and camera-captured documents, addressing existing challenges in the field.

items.title: Beyond Visual Evidence: Revealing and Mitigating Relational Privacy Leakage in Document MLLMs
items.summary: This study explores and proposes methods to mitigate relational privacy leakage in document Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly focusing on their unique vulnerabilities in identity document processing.

items.title: A Deep RL based Framework for Targeted White Matter Tractography
items.summary: This paper proposes a Deep Reinforcement Learning-based framework for targeted white matter tractography, aiming to reconstruct the brain's structural pathways more effectively for neuroimaging applications.

items.title: DiCoR: Decoupled Referent Disambiguation and Contour Recalibration for Efficient Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
items.summary: DiCoR is presented as a method for efficient referring remote sensing image segmentation, which decouples referent disambiguation and contour recalibration to delineate targets specified by natural language.

items.title: PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels
items.summary: This research analyzes PixSDS, explaining why latent Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) causes noisy pixels in text-to-3D generation due to VAE-induced pixel drift.

items.title: Structure-aware Riemannian Growth Fields for 4D Plant Modeling
items.summary: This paper introduces a novel framework using structure-aware Riemannian Growth Fields for 4D plant modeling, reconstructing continuous geometric and topological plant evolution from sparse temporal observations.

items.title: UniTraffic-Agent: Unified Traffic Video Reasoning for AI City Challenge 2026 Track 3 with Two Out-of-Domain Evaluations
items.summary: UniTraffic-Agent is introduced as a unified traffic video reasoning system for the AI City Challenge, designed to understand and explain traffic events in intelligent transportation.

items.title: P2Fusion: Prompt-based Progressive Infrared-Visible Image Fusion via Dual-Prior Distillation
items.summary: P2Fusion proposes a prompt-based progressive infrared-visible image fusion method that uses dual-prior distillation to reconcile information disparity for multimodal perception, addressing limitations of static constraints.

items.title: Topology-Unified 2D Pose Estimation across Intact, Residual and Prosthetic Limbs
items.summary: This paper presents a topology-unified 2D pose estimation method that addresses representation bias in benchmarks by enabling accurate pose estimation across individuals with intact, residual, and prosthetic limbs.

items.title: Learning Unified Video and Image Representation for Video Face Forgery Detection
items.summary: This research focuses on learning unified video and image representations to improve video face forgery detection, aiming to preserve the security and integrity of facial data against deep generative models.

items.title: QuISE: Defense against Typographic Attacks on VLMs via Query-Irrelevant Semantic Editing
items.summary: This research introduces QuISE, a defense mechanism against typographic attacks that trick Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by injecting misleading text into images. The method aims to prevent models from relying on adversarial textual cues instead of visual evidence without requiring extensive model modifications or retraining.

items.title: Predicting Signed Distance Functions for Visual Instance Segmentation
items.summary: This research proposes a method for visual instance segmentation that predicts Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) to better handle objects with unconstrained shapes. It aims to improve segmentation accuracy for items that are not well described by traditional bounding box approaches, such as long or slender objects.

items.title: MergeOver: Post-Training Token Merging for Recursive Vision Transformers
items.summary: MergeOver is presented as a post-training token merging technique designed to reduce the quadratic computational complexity and large parameter counts of Vision Transformers (ViTs). This method aims to enable the deployment of high-performing ViTs on resource-constrained edge hardware.

items.title: A Controlled Study of Self-Supervised Image and Video Pretraining under Limited Resources
items.summary: This research presents a controlled study investigating the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining for visual foundation models under limited data and computational resources. The goal is to determine if significant benefits can be achieved with more sustainable pretraining scales, rather than requiring vast data and compute.

items.title: Temporal GRPO: Beyond Trajectory-Level Credit in Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces Temporal GRPO, a method that refines credit assignment in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) reinforcement learning beyond trajectory-level advantages. It aims to improve outcome-driven post-training of VLA policies from sparse task-success feedback.

items.title: Semantic Radiance Fields as Simulators for Spatial Reasoning in Real-World Scenes
items.summary: This research proposes using Semantic Radiance Fields as simulators to train and evaluate spatial reasoning in embodied agents within real-world scenes. The method aims to provide diverse environments that are both geometrically faithful and semantically queryable, overcoming limitations of purely synthetic or reconstructed simulators.

items.title: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations
items.summary: This research explores methods for decoding task progress directly from internal representations within Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, applying mechanistic interpretability to understand their internal workings and monitor runtime.

items.title: Trajectory Prediction via Bayesian Intention Inference under Unknown Goals and Kinematics
items.summary: This work introduces an adaptive Bayesian algorithm for real-time trajectory prediction, inferring a target's intentions and motion characteristics even when these are unknown and subject to change.

items.title: Training Non-Differentiable Networks via Optimal Transport
items.summary: This research explores a new method for training non-differentiable networks by optimizing losses that exhibit jumps, where traditional backpropagation methods are ineffective.

items.title: Samsung Uses Claude AI to Slash Month-Long Chip Design Tasks to Just Days, But Humans Remain Key - Android Headlines
items.summary: Samsung is using Anthropic's Claude AI to significantly reduce the time required for chip design tasks, transforming processes that previously took months into just days.

items.title: Razorpay’s ChatGPT Gambit, Snapchat’s Next Big Quest & More
items.summary: Razorpay is exploring integrating Indian brands within ChatGPT to establish it as a new commerce channel.

items.title: Can Razorpay Turn ChatGPT Into India’s Next Commerce Channel?

items.summary: A new project, 'Relational-to-KV', uses AI to map relational data models to Key-Value databases like ToplingDB and RocksDB, showcasing an application of AI in data engineering.

items.summary: Recast is utilizing a hyper-resolution AI weather model for its operations, representing an application of AI in scientific modeling.
