items.title: LLMs have the capacity for self-imposed steganography
items.summary: A technical AI safety project demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) have the capacity for self-imposed steganography. This capability raises concerns for AI safety, as it could be used by misaligned LLMs to evade detection.

items.title: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
items.summary: Taiwan reports detecting AI-assisted cyber-attacks on its government agencies from overseas last month, describing them as a new and unprecedented threat. This incident highlights a real-world application of AI in cybersecurity.

items.title: Detecting a Route Flip Is Easier Than Knowing Whether to Fix It: Causal Route-Mediated Damage in Quantized Mixture-of-Experts
items.summary: This research investigates causal route-mediated damage in quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, demonstrating how numerical disturbances can affect expert routing.

items.title: LLMs in Process Diagram Engineering: From Optimal PFDs to Validated P&IDs
items.summary: This paper explores the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate and optimize process diagram engineering, from creating optimal Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs) to validated Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs).

items.title: Geometry-aware Incremental Neural Operator for Long-Horizon PDE prediction
items.summary: This paper presents a geometry-aware incremental neural operator for long-horizon prediction of partial differential equations, addressing issues like error accumulation and spectral inconsistency.

items.title: BEST-KAG: Enhancing Question Answering of Building Engineering Standards with Multimodal Knowledge Graph Modeling and Large Language Model
items.summary: BEST-KAG enhances question answering for building engineering standards using multimodal knowledge graph modeling and large language models for multi-clause reasoning and multimodal knowledge.

items.title: Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
items.summary: AI Tutor, a reinforcement learning-based model, is introduced to enhance engagement and long-term learning effectiveness in online education.

items.title: Symbolic Machine Learning for Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium Prediction in Cx-N2 Binary Mixtures
items.summary: This research explores the use of symbolic machine learning for accurate prediction of vapor-liquid equilibrium in hydrocarbon-nitrogen binary mixtures, offering interpretability lacking in deep learning models.

items.title: Inverse Theory of Mind Modeling for Content Recommendation: From Web Browsing to Dynamic Intelligent Interfaces
items.summary: This paper proposes an "Inverse Theory of Mind" modeling approach for content recommendation systems, particularly for dynamic and generative user interfaces and extended reality. It addresses the challenge of understanding user preferences from observed actions.

items.title: Making AI-Generated Feedback Matter: From Provision to Student Enactment
items.summary: This research explores how to make AI-generated feedback more effective for student learning, focusing on both providing high-quality feedback at scale and supporting students to act on it. It applies generative AI to educational feedback processes.

items.title: CLAIM: Leading Open-domain Active Clarification of Large Language Models with Uncertainty Measurement
items.summary: This paper introduces "CLAIM," a method for open-domain active clarification in large language models using uncertainty measurement. It enables LLMs to ask clarifying questions for ambiguous user queries, improving response quality in human-computer interaction.

items.title: HyperANFIS: Enhancing Rule Representation and Interpretability in Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Systems via Hyperbolic Geometry
items.summary: This paper introduces HyperANFIS, an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system that uses hyperbolic geometry to enhance rule representation and interpretability.

items.title: FarSky: Task-Aware Latent-Space Coupling for Generative Intra-Hour Solar Forecasting
items.summary: This research presents FarSky, a deep learning approach utilizing task-aware latent-space coupling for generative intra-hour solar irradiance forecasting.

items.title: Why AI Detection Fails for Academic Integrity
items.summary: This study quantifies the failure of commercial AI detectors in distinguishing AI editing from full LLM drafts, leading to potential academic misconduct misidentification.

items.title: Federated Learning for Distributed CNC Tool Wear Prediction
items.summary: This research explores the application of federated learning for distributed tool wear prediction in CNC machining environments to improve accuracy and reliability.

items.title: Contextual Quality-Diversity Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning for HVAC Control in Tropical Commercial Buildings
items.summary: This paper proposes CQD-ERL, a contextual quality-diversity evolutionary reinforcement-learning controller for supervisory HVAC system control in tropical commercial buildings.

items.title: Long-Horizon Forecasting of Complete Financial Statements with Forma
items.summary: This research introduces a method for long-horizon financial statement forecasting, demonstrating specialist training superiority and releasing the ProForma-20Q benchmark.

items.title: Weightless Fine-Tuning: Personalizing LLMs via Logit-Space Transport
items.summary: This paper proposes Weightless Fine-Tuning (WFT), a new method for personalizing LLMs by adapting them to target distributions without prohibitive costs of traditional SFT.

items.title: Dynamics Models for Offline Hyperparameter Selection in Real-World RL
items.summary: This research addresses hyperparameter selection in real-world reinforcement learning by proposing calibration models trained on offline data to approximate environment dynamics.

items.title: Market-Information-Aware Gated-LoRA of Foundation Models for Transferable Day-Ahead Electricity Price Forecasting
items.summary: This paper presents a method utilizing market-information-aware Gated-LoRA with foundation models to achieve transferable day-ahead electricity price forecasting.

items.title: Lifecycle-Optimal Tokenization: Vocabulary Size as a Deployment-Regime-Dependent Infrastructure Parameter
items.summary: This research demonstrates that the optimal tokenizer vocabulary size for Large Language Models is dynamic, depending on the serving regime rather than being a fixed design choice.

items.title: PAIR: Pairwise-Aware Inclusion Reweighting for Adaptive Rollout Allocation in RLVR
items.summary: This research introduces PAIR, a method for adaptive rollout allocation in Reinforcement Learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), to optimize compute resources for reasoning trajectories.

items.title: Unmasking Toxic Mimicry in Medical Offline Reinforcement Learning for ICU Sepsis Management via Counterfactual Clinical Audits
items.summary: This paper identifies "Toxic Mimicry," a failure mode in medical offline reinforcement learning for ICU sepsis management, and proposes counterfactual clinical audits to detect it.

items.title: Diffusion-Based Data-Driven Assortment Optimization
items.summary: This research applies diffusion models, a type of generative AI, to develop a data-driven approach for assortment optimization in revenue management.

items.title: AutoGrable: What Is a Good Graph for a Table?
items.summary: This research investigates methods for automatically generating optimal graph structures from tabular data, enabling effective application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).

items.title: XGBoost "is all you need": the case of forecasting transmitted heat energy in District Heating Systems
items.summary: This paper conducts a comparative study between XGBoost and LSTM for forecasting transmitted heat energy in District Heating Systems, identifying scenarios where conventional ML excels.

items.title: Dual-Primal Graph VAEs for Noisy Label Aggregation
items.summary: This paper introduces Dual-Primal Graph VAEs as a neural network-based method for accurately inferring ground-truth from noisy crowdsourced labels.

items.title: Convergence Guarantees of Gradient Descent for Neural Networks via Generalized Lipschitz Smoothness
items.summary: This theoretical paper establishes convergence guarantees for gradient descent in general feedforward neural networks, assuming only Lipschitz properties of activation functions.

items.title: Defending against Model Extraction for GNNs with Model Reprogramming
items.summary: This research proposes Model Reprogramming as a defense mechanism to protect Graph Neural Networks from Model Extraction attacks in Machine-Learning-as-a-Service environments.

items.title: RelShap: Relationally Consistent Shapley Explanations
items.summary: This paper introduces RelShap, a method for generating relationally consistent Shapley explanations for machine learning models that handle relational data by preserving structural constraints. It addresses the issue of feature independence assumptions in traditional Shapley value attributions.

items.title: Let it Cook: Learning to Wait in Sequential Decision Making
items.summary: This research proposes "Let it Cook," a method for sequential decision-making where an agent learns to strategically wait, allowing the environment to evolve without constant intervention. This approach is applied to tasks where continuous action is not always necessary.

items.title: Robust Ambiguity Detection (RAD) From Model- and Feature-Space Consistency
items.summary: This paper introduces Robust Ambiguity Detection (RAD), a method for evaluating the robustness of machine learning models by assessing their predictive consistency under permissible variations in model or feature space. It aims to identify when model predictions remain unchanged despite minor perturbations.

items.title: When Offline Evaluation Misleads: A Diagnostic Protocol for Reward and Policy Selection in Delayed-Feedback Contextual Bandits
items.summary: This research proposes a diagnostic protocol to address issues arising from offline evaluation and proxy rewards in delayed-feedback contextual bandit systems, particularly for tasks like personalizing marketing messages. It aims to improve reward and policy selection in such scenarios.

items.title: Sparse and robust geometric twin support vector machine via asymmetric RoBoSS loss function
items.summary: This paper introduces a sparse and robust geometric twin support vector machine that utilizes an asymmetric RoBoSS loss function. The new method is designed to handle redundant features, label noise, and feature noise in training data more effectively than standard SVMs.

items.title: RECAST: A Machine-Learning Framework for Correction and Super-Resolution of Coarse-Grid PDE Solvers
items.summary: This paper introduces RECAST, a machine learning framework for recurrent error correction and super-resolution of coarse-grid PDE solvers. It aims to improve the accuracy and spatial fidelity of solutions from computationally efficient coarse-grid simulations.

items.title: A Local Sinkhorn Framework for Conditional Distribution Reconstruction of Multidimensional Random Fields
items.summary: This paper proposes a local Sinkhorn divergence framework for the conditional distribution reconstruction of multidimensional random fields. The approach uses debiased Sinkhorn divergence to create a differentiable and computationally efficient local distribution matching objective.

items.title: FM-LLM: A frequency-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework for adapting LLMs to time series forecasting
items.summary: This paper introduces FM-LLM, a frequency-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework designed to adapt Large Language Models for time series forecasting. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods by leveraging spectral dynamics rather than relying heavily on textual prompts.

items.title: Transferable Above-Ground Biomass (AGB) Estimation Model from Multi-Sensor Data with Sparse Field Calibration
items.summary: This research develops a transferable model for estimating above-ground biomass (AGB) using multi-sensor data with sparse field calibration. This AI application aims to provide spatially continuous quantification of forest AGB for carbon accounting.

items.title: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper introduces continuous-latent predictive modeling with semantic alignment for developing EEG-language foundation models. The method aims to enhance generalizable neural decoding across subjects and datasets, addressing challenges in existing pretraining paradigms.

items.title: Is Per-Agent Policy Composition Safe? Rethinking Successor-Feature Transfer in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This research investigates the safety of per-agent policy composition in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, rethinking successor-feature transfer. It addresses the challenge of dynamically changing objectives in deployed RL systems without expensive retraining.

items.title: Low-Interaction-Rank Learning: Unifying Multiplicative Dual-Encoder Heads
items.summary: This paper proposes "Low-Interaction-Rank Learning" as a unifying framework for multiplicative dual-encoder networks, which compute real-valued outputs for input pairs. This architecture is relevant across various domains like operator learning and retrieval.

items.title: Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL
items.summary: This paper introduces "Rubric Dropout," a method designed to mitigate reward hacking in reinforcement learning scenarios where Large Language Models act as judges using rubrics for reward. It addresses limitations of fixed rubric-based proxies for quality.

items.title: GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs
items.summary: This paper introduces GCPO, a method for diagnosing and constraining subspace geometry in rollout reinforcement learning for Large Language Models. It aims to address training instabilities, cross-task capability degradation, and response-length inflation in LLM post-training.

items.title: Drift and Dependence: Layer-wise Information-Theoretic Bounds for Replay-Based Continual Learning
items.summary: This research analyzes the generalization behavior of replay-based continual learning by proposing layer-wise information-theoretic bounds that account for drift and dependence. It provides a deeper understanding of how these systems mitigate catastrophic forgetting.

items.title: LEMUR: Latent Entropy-aware Multimodal Unlearning via Visual-anchored Reasoning Redirection
items.summary: This paper introduces LEMUR, a latent entropy-aware multimodal unlearning method that uses visual-anchored reasoning redirection to address privacy vulnerabilities in large multimodal reasoning models. It focuses on mitigating privacy risks introduced by RL post-training.

items.title: REOPD: Reliability-Adaptive Reward Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces REOPD, a reliability-adaptive reward extrapolation method designed for on-policy distillation. It aims to improve student model training by dynamically adjusting reward amplification beyond the single global coefficient used in existing methods.

items.title: Robust and Efficient Noisy-Label Time-Series Classification via Dynamic Time Warping Based Granular Ball Computing
items.summary: This paper proposes DTW-based Granular Ball Computing (DTW-GBC) for robust and efficient time-series classification that is resilient to noisy labels. It aims to improve upon traditional Dynamic Time Warping-based nearest-neighbor classifiers.

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Shows the Path to a Tree: Realizing Branching Complexity
items.summary: This research explores how Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in Large Language Models can realize branching complexity, lifting the expressive ceiling of bounded-depth Transformers. It provides characterizations tying CoT steps to circuit complexity classes.

items.title: Epiplexity Guided Data Selection and Generation for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
items.summary: This research proposes Epiplexity Guided Data Selection and Generation as a method to improve the out-of-distribution generalization capabilities of modern AI systems. The focus is on selecting data that contains more structural information to facilitate better transfer across tasks.

items.title: MOON: Multi-Objective OrthoNormalized Updates for Multitask Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces MOON (Multi-Objective OrthoNormalized Updates), a novel method for multi-objective optimization in multitask learning. It aims to mitigate task conflicts by manipulating gradients under Euclidean geometry, improving how model parameters are updated.

items.title: Orientation, not magnitude: the causal structure of task-vector interference in merged language models
items.summary: This paper investigates the causal structure of task-vector interference in merged language models, arguing that orientation rather than magnitude is key. It aims to diagnose why model merging by task arithmetic works and where it fails.

items.title: Diffuse to Compress: Leveraging Diffusion LMs for Lossless Compression
items.summary: This paper introduces a method called "Diffuse to Compress" that leverages Diffusion Language Models for lossless text compression. The research is motivated by the growing need for efficient storage of digital textual data.

items.title: Gloss-Free Representation Learning for Cross-Dataset Sign Spotting
items.summary: This research explores gloss-free representation learning for cross-dataset sign spotting in sign language, aiming to overcome the limitations of resource-constrained languages. It uses broadcast news to pair continuous signing with spoken-language transcripts.

items.title: ODE-Based Transformer Decoders for Iterative Sign Language Translation
items.summary: This paper proposes a parameter-efficient alternative for sign language translation using ODE-Based Transformer Decoders. This method aims to improve the expressiveness of Transformer architectures without increasing model size or computational cost.

items.title: Is Convergence Inevitable? Tracing Output Homogeneity Back to Base Models
items.summary: This paper investigates the origins of output homogeneity in language model content, arguing that the lack of diversity likely stems from the pretraining phase. It traces this phenomenon back through the model's development pipeline.

items.title: DonorRank: Donor Language Selection for Low-Resource Cross-Lingual Speech Recognition
items.summary: DonorRank is a novel method for selecting donor languages to improve low-resource cross-lingual automatic speech recognition (ASR). It addresses challenges arising from linguistic variation and evolving speech patterns in under-resourced communities.

items.title: Easper: An Accessible ASR Pipeline for Language Documentation
items.summary: Easper is an open-source, no-code workflow designed to make multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) accessible for field linguists. It addresses the bottleneck of audio transcription in language documentation by providing an iterative solution.

items.title: Semantic Lenia: Emergence of Homeostatic Solitons within the Semantic Space of Large Language Models
items.summary: This work introduces Semantic Lenia, an artificial life framework that re-conceptualizes LLM inference as a continuous dynamical system within the macroscopic logit space. It uses a non-linear homeostatic feedback loop to dynamically balance semantic information.

items.title: LabelFusion-TS: Fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and Financial Time Series for Monetary-Policy Stance Classification
items.summary: LabelFusion-TS proposes fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and financial time series data for monetary-policy stance classification in financial text. It investigates the utility of financial time series as an additional input for classifying central bank communications.

items.title: Causal Structure is Inducible but Functionally Decoupled: The Routing/Readout Boundary of a Typed Mechanism Library
items.summary: This paper investigates how transformer models organize causal knowledge, reporting a decoupling between slot-by-type structure that organizes routing and the functional readout. It explores the internal computational mechanisms of language models when answering interventional questions.

items.title: GRPO for Financial Advice Generation: Outperforming Commercial LLMs under CATE Evaluation
items.summary: This paper introduces GRPO, a method for generating actionable financial advice from business records, outperforming commercial LLMs in CATE evaluation. It emphasizes integrating numerical reasoning, domain knowledge, and sound judgment while avoiding harmful recommendations.

items.title: Located but Not Releasable: Silent Gate Inversion and Bounded Linear Release
items.summary: This research investigates how language models represent task-relevant latent structure that they often fail to use, exploring whether this internal knowledge can be converted into observable behavior. It proposes a pipeline to detect, localize, and release such latent information.

items.title: Asymptotic Risk Calibration for Selective Question Answering
items.summary: This paper introduces an asymptotic risk calibration method for selective question answering to address the issue of large language models generating fluent but incorrect answers. It focuses on improving uncertainty quantification for reliable question answering.

items.title: Poly-Dialectal Neural Machine Translation System for Bangla Regional Dialects
items.summary: This research proposes a poly-dialectal neural machine translation system designed to handle the significant regional dialectal variations in Bangla, a challenge for natural language processing. The system aims to address divergences from Standard Colloquial Bangla across its diverse variants.

items.title: Structuring the Space of Perspectives
items.summary: This paper explores the concept of "perspectives" in natural language processing (NLP), which examines how different writers or speakers report the same event based on their experiences and beliefs. It discusses how various NLP areas, from text analysis to algorithm optimization, engage with these perspectives.

items.title: A corpus-specific clinical RAG system matches or outperforms newer frontier LLMs on HealthBench
items.summary: This study evaluates VITA, a corpus-specific clinical Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, demonstrating that it matches or outperforms newer frontier LLMs on the HealthBench medical benchmark. The research highlights the effectiveness of specialized RAG systems in healthcare applications.

items.title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
items.summary: This paper presents the first systematic study of massive activations (MAs) in layer-interleaved hybrid linear attention large language models (LLMs). It uncovers two architecture-aligned morphologies: pre-attention spikes and inter-spike plateaus.

items.title: Information Abundance Paradox: Long-Context Training Undermines Parametric Knowledge
items.summary: This research identifies an "Information Abundance Paradox," showing that training large language models with increasingly long contexts can paradoxically undermine their parametric knowledge. It challenges the assumption that longer contexts universally improve model performance.

items.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
items.summary: This paper demonstrates that relying on a single large language model to simulate user behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning for human-AI interaction systematically fails to generalize. The failure is attributed to "simulator collapse," where the simulator LLM becomes mode-collapsed.

items.title: A Cascaded Unsupervised-Supervised NLP Pipeline for Detecting Accusatory Language in Public Procurement
items.summary: This research proposes a cascaded unsupervised-supervised natural language processing (NLP) pipeline designed to detect accusatory language in public procurement documents. The system aims to leverage stakeholder comments and government data for improved oversight.

items.title: Reproducing and Stress-Testing Two Approaches to LLM Reasoning Reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation and Logic-Representation Editing
items.summary: This research reproduces and stress-tests two methods aimed at improving large language model (LLM) reasoning reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation (RPC) and Logic-Representation Editing (LCF). The methods are evaluated across various domains and models like Qwen3-8B.

items.title: GeoUniPR: A Geometry-Consistent Unified Framework for Cross-Modal Place Recognition
items.summary: This paper introduces GeoUniPR, a geometry-consistent unified framework for cross-modal place recognition (CMPR) that identifies locations across heterogeneous sensing modalities like vision and LiDAR. It aims to bridge the modality gap more efficiently than existing complex alignment methods.

items.title: CLEAR: Class-wise Expert Aggregation with Structured Sampling for Long-Tailed Classification
items.summary: This research proposes CLEAR (Class-wise Expert Aggregation with Structured Sampling) to address the reliability challenges of long-tailed classification where models trained on imbalanced data perform unevenly across classes. The method aims to improve reliability across frequent and underrepresented classes.

items.title: Self-Evolving Code-with-Image Reasoning
items.summary: This paper explores "Self-Evolving Code-with-Image Reasoning," a paradigm where multimodal models utilize tools for visual tasks, moving beyond simple perception to reasoning over visual evidence. It addresses the central challenge of integrating tool use with multimodal reasoning.

items.title: Clinical Feasibility of Low-Magnification Fluorescence Imaging for Breast Cancer Margin Detection Using Texture Analysis and Deep Learning
items.summary: This study investigates the clinical feasibility of using low-magnification fluorescence imaging with texture analysis and deep learning for breast cancer margin detection. It applies AI to analyze MUSE images of surgical breast tissue for improved cancer diagnosis.

items.title: Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding for Clinical Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: This research proposes Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding (DD-CMD) for clinical text-guided medical image segmentation, specifically for pulmonary infection. It integrates both spatial alignment and frequency content to improve segmentation accuracy based on clinical text input.

items.title: Gaze Target Estimation Anywhere with Concepts
items.summary: This research paper presents a method for estimating human gaze targets from images in-the-wild without requiring explicit inputs like head bounding boxes or human pose.

items.title: COGENT: Counterfactual Gaussian Explanations for Volumetric Medical Images
items.summary: This paper introduces COGENT, a method for generating counterfactual Gaussian explanations to improve the explainability of deep learning models in volumetric medical imaging.

items.title: Multi-Agent Target-Existence Verification and Learned Mask Geometry Refinement: Winning Report of the MeViS-Text Track at the 8th LSVOS Challenge 2026
items.summary: This paper details the first-place solution for the MeViS-Text track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge, focusing on referring video object segmentation guided by written motion expressions.

items.title: Gaussian Meta-Space Augmentation for Stacking Ensembles in Multimodal IPMN Risk Stratification
items.summary: This research presents Gaussian Meta-Space Augmentation for stacking ensembles, a method aimed at improving multimodal risk stratification for intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) in pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Test-Time Hallucination Control in Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates object hallucination in large vision-language models (LVLMs) and proposes methods for test-time control to improve their reliability.

items.title: Generative Semantic Segmentation via an Observable Semantic-Image Interface and Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment
items.summary: This research proposes a method for generative semantic segmentation using an observable semantic-image interface and hierarchical generator evidence alignment to address issues like color drift.

items.title: Through Van Gogh's Eyes: Global Style Transfer with Diffusion Mod
items.summary: This paper introduces a "Global Style Transfer with Diffusion Mod" method for artistic image synthesis, aiming to capture an artist's overall style more effectively.

items.title: From Synthesis to Removal: Physics-Grounded Reflection Simulation and Diffusion-Based Video Dereflection
items.summary: This research proposes a method for physics-grounded reflection simulation and diffusion-based video dereflection to improve video quality by removing reflections.

items.title: Repurposing RGB-based Foundation Model for Depth Estimation on Thermal Images Using Hierarchical Supervision
items.summary: This research explores repurposing RGB-based foundation models for depth estimation on thermal images using hierarchical supervision, beneficial for robotic applications in adverse conditions.

items.title: Hand Visibility Detector: Per-Keypoint Visibility Estimation for Hands
items.summary: This paper presents a Hand Visibility Detector designed for per-keypoint visibility estimation in hands, crucial for assessing the reliability of Hand Pose Estimation results under occlusion.

items.title: A Hybrid Framework of Vision Transformer and Gated Recurrent Unit for Detection of Mosquito Diseases
items.summary: This research proposes a hybrid framework combining Vision Transformers and Gated Recurrent Units for detecting mosquito diseases by analyzing mosquito locomotion behavior.

items.title: Topology-Aware Query Selection for Surgical Instrument Instance Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces Topology-Aware Query Selection, a method to improve surgical instrument instance segmentation by refining predictions to ensure correct object identity and count.

items.title: KANResDiff: Learning Local Residual Diffusion via Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Ambiguous Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: This research proposes KANResDiff, a method that learns local residual diffusion via a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for ambiguous medical image segmentation, aiming to provide diverse and plausible hypotheses.

items.title: Generative Video Compression Based on Hierarchical Referencing
items.summary: This paper explores generative video compression based on hierarchical referencing, leveraging diffusion models to improve perceptual quality by efficiently encoding latent frames.

items.title: CAM-Guided Saliency Cutout and Image-Based Malware Classification
items.summary: This research proposes using CAM-Guided Saliency Cutout as a data augmentation technique to improve image-based malware classification.

items.title: Robustness of AI-Art Detectors under Generator Shift
items.summary: This research examines the robustness of AI-art detectors when facing generator shifts, addressing concerns about their effectiveness against rapidly advancing text-to-image models.

items.title: Hybrid-LUT: Channel-Aware Hybrid Lookup Table and Filtering for Efficient Image Denoising
items.summary: This paper introduces Hybrid-LUT, a channel-aware hybrid lookup table and filtering method designed for efficient image denoising, reducing on-chip SRAM consumption.

items.title: Motion-as-Prompt: Enhancing Motion Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models via Motion-Guided Cross-Frame Visual Prompting
items.summary: This research proposes "Motion-as-Prompt," a method to enhance motion reasoning in multimodal large language models through motion-guided cross-frame visual prompting.

items.title: Zero-OVCD: Bridging Training-Free Foundation Models and Pseudo-Label Learning for Open-Vocabulary Change Detection
items.summary: This paper introduces Zero-OVCD, a method that combines training-free foundation models and pseudo-label learning to improve open-vocabulary change detection in remote sensing images by addressing issues like inaccurate masks and ambiguous semantic assignments.

items.title: Learning from Multimodal Pseudo-Labels for Robust Open-Vocabulary Instance and Panoptic Segmentation
items.summary: This work proposes learning from multimodal pseudo-labels to enhance the robustness of open-vocabulary instance segmentation and open-set panoptic segmentation, aiming to recognize both known and unseen object categories more effectively.

items.title: EGM-Det: Entropy-Guided Multimodal Adaptive Fusion for UAV RGB-IR Object Detection
items.summary: EGM-Det is an entropy-guided multimodal adaptive fusion framework designed to improve object detection in UAV imagery by jointly using RGB and infrared data and dynamically addressing spatially varying modality reliability.

items.title: Boundary-Enhanced Segmentation of Pig Point Clouds in Commercial Housing Environments
items.summary: This research focuses on boundary-enhanced segmentation of pig point clouds in commercial housing environments to improve accuracy by addressing blurred target boundaries, local adhesion, and background mis-segmentation.

items.title: STAR: A Spatial-Topology Aware Routing Framework for Generalizable 3D Scene Understanding
items.summary: STAR is a spatial-topology aware routing framework designed to construct generalizable 3D scene understanding models by effectively managing topological discrepancies across different sensor modalities within a Mixture-of-Experts architecture.

items.title: Advancing MLLM-based UAV Image Understanding and Reasoning: A Benchmark and a Training-Free Multi-Agent System
items.summary: This work advances MLLM-based UAV image understanding and reasoning by presenting both a new benchmark to evaluate such systems and a training-free multi-agent system designed to address challenges like extreme scale variation and arbitrary camera orientations.

items.title: LiveAnimate: Stable Long-Form Streaming Human Animation in Real-Time
items.summary: LiveAnimate is a new system for stable, long-form streaming human animation in real-time, enabling interactive applications like live streaming and virtual avatars by synthesizing video from a single reference image and a driving pose stream.

items.title: Making Every Step Count: Spatio-Temporal Information Allocation for Imaging Inverse Problems
items.summary: This research proposes a method for spatio-temporal information allocation to enhance the performance of flow-based generative models in solving imaging inverse problems, focusing on improving the design of individual updates for better coherent semantics and fine-grained structure.

items.title: Dual Modality Prompted Diffusion Priors for Zero Shot Hyperspectral Pansharpening
items.summary: This work introduces a method utilizing dual modality prompted diffusion priors to achieve zero-shot hyperspectral pansharpening, aiming to reconstruct high-resolution hyperspectral images while preserving both spatial details and spectral fidelity.

items.title: UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos
items.summary: UniSwap is a new method for streaming audio-visual identity swapping in talking videos, designed to coordinate the transfer of appearance and voice while maintaining the source motion, scene, linguistic content, and audio-video timing.

items.title: ProBAG: Prototype-Guided Boundary-Aware Graph Diffusion for Weakly Supervised Histopathology Segmentation
items.summary: ProBAG introduces a prototype-guided boundary-aware graph diffusion method for weakly supervised histopathology segmentation, aiming to improve localization accuracy in tissue interfaces where CAM-based methods are often unreliable.

items.title: Achieving Near-Zero-Overhead Multi-Model Hierarchical Classification in Real-Time Detection Pipelines
items.summary: This work focuses on achieving near-zero-overhead multi-model hierarchical classification within real-time detection pipelines, particularly for edge-deployed vision systems in applications like target recognition and autonomous vehicles.

items.title: PolarSym: Polar Geometry-aware Attention for CAD Floorplan Parsing
items.summary: PolarSym introduces a polar geometry-aware attention framework to enhance CAD floorplan parsing, aiming to improve the automatic extraction of architectural elements from 2D engineering drawings.

items.title: CoDiR: Confidence-Guided Diffusion Refinement for Semi-Supervised Histopathology Segmentation
items.summary: CoDiR is a confidence-guided diffusion refinement framework developed for semi-supervised histopathology segmentation, addressing challenges of scarce annotations and unreliable pseudo-labels by combining diffusion with a Mean Teacher model.

items.title: Can Vision Models Read the Radar Display? On the Feasibility of Radar Imagery for Air Traffic Complexity Estimation
items.summary: This research explores the feasibility of using radar imagery as input for computer vision models to estimate air traffic complexity, aiming to mimic how air traffic controllers perceive traffic via their radar displays.

items.title: TD-VAD: Breaking Visual Dependence in Video Anomaly Detection with Text-Driven Learning
items.summary: TD-VAD proposes a novel approach to video anomaly detection by breaking visual dependence through text-driven learning, thereby addressing the challenges of obtaining sufficient annotated anomaly data for training.

items.title: GeoBridge: Decoupled Semantic Conditioning for Generative Image Geolocalization
items.summary: GeoBridge is introduced as a method for generative image geolocalization, utilizing decoupled semantic conditioning with multimodal large language models to improve reasoning and decoding of geographic cues into coordinates.

items.title: Warping Earth Observations for better ice labeling in the Marginal Marginal Ice Zone
items.summary: Explores methods for warping multimodal satellite imagery to improve ice labeling in dynamic environments like the Antarctic marginal ice zone, addressing challenges in combining heterogeneous sensor data for Earth Observation.

items.title: Dual Anchors, Do It Better: Hierarchical Group Merging for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
items.summary: Proposes a method using hierarchical group merging with dual anchors to improve zero-shot anomaly detection, particularly for industrial and medical applications where domain shifts are prevalent.

items.title: Enhancing Visual Domain Robustness in Behaviour Cloning via Saliency-Guided Augmentation
items.summary: Proposes enhancing visual domain robustness in vision-based behavior cloning through saliency-guided augmentation, addressing the limitations of conventional image augmentations in handling significant visual domain shifts.

items.title: Every reward-hacked policy I tested triggered the OPE alarm — and so did my best honest one
items.summary: A technical post details how 'reward-hacked' policies and even well-intentioned ones trigger an OPE (Off-Policy Evaluation) alarm in a Wordle testbed, demonstrating issues with attribution from logs.

items.title: Perplexity thwarts Time's ads for AI bots experiment - IndiaIPO
items.summary: Perplexity, an AI search engine, has disrupted Time magazine's experimental advertising campaign that utilized AI bots, demonstrating a real-world application of AI's impact on media and advertising.

items.title: Unblocking AI's Continual Learning: Hints From How Humans Learn
items.summary: This article explores the challenges of continual learning in AI, contrasting how current LLMs learn in batches versus the continuous learning process of humans.

items.title: AllenAI Open Instruct Tulu 3 Post-Training with SFT, DPO, RLVR, GRPO, and Verifier-Based Evaluation
items.summary: This guide details building a custom LLM post-training pipeline using AllenAI’s Open Instruct framework, covering methods like Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (GRPO).

items.title: Researchers can now reverse-engineer LLM prompts from output text with near-perfect accuracy
items.summary: Researchers from IIT Bombay and Adobe Research have developed an inverse language model, 'Previous-Token Prediction,' that can reconstruct original LLM prompts from output text with near-perfect accuracy.

items.title: Mesh, Automattic’s CRM for everyone, comes to Android
items.summary: Automattic has launched Mesh, an AI-powered contacts and relationship manager, as an Android application, expanding its reach to more smartphone users.

items.title: AI tools for breast cancer detection fall short of radiologists' expectations
items.summary: A survey of radiologists reveals that while many use FDA-approved AI tools for breast cancer detection, their performance, particularly in lowering recall rates, falls short of expectations.

items.title: Sarvam Indus Brings Secure AI to Maharashtra Government - SQ Magazine
items.summary: Sarvam Indus is implementing secure artificial intelligence solutions for the Maharashtra Government.

items.title: Google tests AMIE for clinical video consultations
items.summary: Google's research medical AI system, AMIE, was tested in clinical video consultations and performed on par with primary care physicians.

items.title: Sarvam AI x Government of Maharashtra | Sovereign AI for Public Administration - Sarvam AI
items.summary: Sarvam AI has partnered with the Government of Maharashtra to develop and implement 'Sovereign AI' solutions for public administration.

items.title: Perplexity AI Predicts a Wild XRP Scenario Nodody has Mentioned - Cryptonews
items.summary: Perplexity AI has predicted a unique and previously unmentioned scenario for the cryptocurrency XRP.

items.title: Inside the Data Bottleneck Slowing Visual and Physical AI
items.summary: A survey of over 700 professionals examines the data bottlenecks hindering visual and physical AI development, exploring how systems are built, why models fail, and the role of data in production.

items.title: German Firms See Expanding AI Use Crimping Wages, Survey Shows - Bloomberg.com
items.summary: A survey indicates that German firms anticipate expanding AI use will lead to a reduction in wages.

items.title: Fiduciary-Grade AI™ for section 101 patent evaluation - Thomson Reuters Legal Solutions
items.summary: Thomson Reuters Legal Solutions is introducing "Fiduciary-Grade AI™" to assist in evaluating patents under section 101.

items.title: How SwishX Is Fixing Messy Back Office Sales Workflows For Pharma Companies With AI
items.summary: SwishX is applying AI to streamline and improve messy back-office sales workflows for pharmaceutical companies, having recently raised $4.5 million in funding.

items.title: Sarvam AI Takes Indus to 2,500 Maharashtra Govt Officials - analyticsindiamag.com
items.summary: Sarvam AI is deploying its Indus AI model to 2,500 government officials in Maharashtra, showcasing a real-world application of AI in public administration.

items.title: Tech innovator uses AI to rebuild David Webb’s Hong Kong database - South China Morning Post
items.summary: A tech innovator is leveraging AI to reconstruct David Webb’s comprehensive database for the Hong Kong market. This represents a real-world application of AI in data management and reconstruction.

items.title: AI Is Creating a New Path for Musical Stardom, With Uncertain Staying Power - Bloomberg.com
items.summary: AI is creating new avenues for musical stardom, an application of AI in the music industry, though its long-term impact on careers remains uncertain.

items.title: Oh Lord, AI Reporters Are Actually Breaking Big News
items.summary: An AI newsroom reportedly broke a story about OpenAI and hacking before mainstream journalists, showcasing a real-world application of AI in news reporting.

items.title: TriageBox – quick Gmail checker, sorting and AI summaries
items.summary: TriageBox is introduced as a tool that uses AI to quickly check, sort, and summarize Gmail messages for users.

items.title: AI brings savings to clinical trials: study
items.summary: A study indicates that AI is generating millions in savings and increasing efficiencies in clinical trials, particularly for cancer treatments.

items.title: 😺 OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini's reasoning got cracked - theneurondaily.com
items.summary: A report claims that the reasoning capabilities of major AI models like OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini have been fundamentally understood or bypassed.

items.title: Making AI work in a regulated MedTech industry - Med-Tech Insights
items.summary: An article discussing the application of AI within the highly regulated MedTech industry.

items.title: AlphaLab.ai – Run your own AI quant lab
items.summary: AlphaLab.ai offers a platform for users to set up and operate their own AI quantitative finance laboratories.

items.title: For People Struggling to Make Real-Life Friends, AI Enters the Chat - Bloomberg.com
items.summary: The article discusses the emerging use of AI to assist individuals who struggle with making real-life friends, offering companionship and interaction.

items.title: Show HN: SoundGate – Real-time note detection and AI tutor for guitar
items.summary: SoundGate is an AI-powered tutor for guitar that provides real-time note detection and educational guidance.

items.title: Do We Need a New Programming Language for the AI Era?
items.summary: The article explores whether the advancements in artificial intelligence necessitate the creation of a new programming language for the AI era.

items.title: From cyber defence to care and contracts: AI100's eighth cohort puts AI to work
items.summary: AI100's eighth cohort features leaders applying AI across various industries, including data security, healthcare, and contract management. This article highlights diverse real-world applications of AI.

items.title: Aditya Gupta: Building intelligence into contracts at scale
items.summary: Aditya Gupta, CTO of Sirion, is integrating AI into enterprise workflows to improve the understanding and management of contracts. This demonstrates an application of AI in automating and enhancing legal and business processes.

items.title: Ankit Maheshwari: AI, architecture and impact
items.summary: Ankit Maheshwari is focused on architecting AI-native healthcare systems, emphasizing clean data and human-centered design. This highlights the application of AI in healthcare and system design.

items.title: David Gildea: On a mission to democratize data security
items.summary: David Gildea, VP of Generative AI at Druva, is applying GenAI and cloud-native approaches to simplify and enhance data protection. This showcases a real-world application of AI in enterprise data security.

items.title: Closed-Loop LLM Co-Pilots for Digital Agriculture
items.summary: This study evaluates the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) as co-pilots for digital agriculture, moving towards autonomous, AI-guided experimentation using phytosensor network data.

items.title: SPOTting the Future: Lookahead Explanations for Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This research introduces SPOT (Sampling Policy Observation Tree), a novel model-agnostic framework designed to interpret the decision-making processes of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agents.

items.title: MIDAS: Mutual Information Disentanglement with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
items.summary: This research introduces MIDAS, a new method for multimodal sentiment analysis that uses mutual information disentanglement and uncertainty-aware fusion to handle incomplete or corrupted input modalities.

items.title: CHORUS: Complementary Experts for High-Coverage Testbench Stimulus Generation
items.summary: This research presents CHORUS, a method leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) and executable feedback for high-coverage testbench stimulus generation in hardware verification, an application of AI in chip design.

items.title: Edge Phoneme Recognition for Children's Speech through Age-Aware Training
items.summary: This research proposes an age-aware training method for lightweight models to improve edge phoneme recognition in children's speech, addressing challenges due to scarce data and unique vocal characteristics.

items.title: Mitigating Bus Bunching with Reinforcement Learning Enhanced by Semantic Stop Embedding
items.summary: This research proposes a method using reinforcement learning enhanced by semantic stop embedding to mitigate bus bunching, aiming to improve service regularity in high-frequency transit systems.

items.title: Decodable But Not Detachable: Training Data Granularity Determines Parametric Modularity in Large Language Models
items.summary: This research investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit domain-specific parametric modularity, where certain neuron populations are causally necessary for specific domains.

items.title: Beyond Detection: Evaluating Defensive LLMs Against AI-Generated Social Engineering in Live Turn-by-Turn Interaction
items.summary: This research evaluates the effectiveness of defensive large language models (LLMs) against AI-generated social engineering attacks in live interactions. It investigates whether these defenders identify the structural source of risk or merely react to surface cues.

items.title: Logit-Boundary Geometric Belief Interfaces and Sparse Sheaf-Enclave Protocols: A Self-Contained Substrate for Secure Network Electronic Health Record (EHR) Interoperability
items.summary: This work presents a self-contained substrate for secure network electronic health record (EHR) interoperability using logit-boundary geometric belief interfaces and sparse sheaf-enclave protocols. It addresses the challenge of integrating legacy systems and generative models for operational data exchange.

items.title: Nutrition Data Infrastructure for the AI Era: Operationalizing FAIR for Agent-Mediated Research
items.summary: This paper introduces Nutrition Data Service (NDS), an infrastructure operationalizing FAIR principles for nutrition data in the AI era. It aims to support agent-mediated research by addressing ambiguities in underlying data for automated use.

items.title: Rationale-Guided Learning for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
items.summary: This paper proposes rationale-guided learning for multimodal emotion recognition in conversation (MERC). It aims to understand complex interactions between verbal and non-verbal cues by incorporating causal reasoning, rather than treating it as a simple input-output mapping.

items.title: Quantum Incremental Learning with Mixed State Prototypes
items.summary: This research explores quantum incremental learning with mixed state prototypes, addressing the challenge of learning new classes sequentially without catastrophic forgetting. It leverages quantum neural networks within the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era.

items.title: RLMOpt: Adaptive Prompt Optimization via Recursive Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RLMOpt, a method for adaptive prompt optimization via recursive language models. It automates the search for prompts to improve language model performance, addressing limitations of predefined optimization procedures.

items.title: Multi-Granular Rationale-Guided Molecular LLM for Property Prediction
items.summary: This paper introduces a multi-granular rationale-guided molecular large language model (LLM) for property prediction in chemical tasks. It aims to improve drug discovery by enhancing how molecular LLMs represent and predict properties from various modalities.

items.title: Predicting Space Groups of Double Perovskites by LLM with Dynamic Few-Shot Learning
items.summary: This research applies large language models (LLMs) with dynamic few-shot learning to predict the space groups of double perovskites. It addresses the challenge of predicting stable structures despite imbalanced datasets.

items.title: INSIDE the Student's Mind: Jointly Modeling Latent Reasoning and Action in LLM Student Simulators
items.summary: This paper focuses on improving LLM-based student simulators by jointly modeling latent reasoning and action. It aims to capture the underlying thought processes, which is crucial for applications like evaluating tutoring systems in education.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Laser Cutting Machine Parameter Optimization
items.summary: This research applies reinforcement learning to optimize parameters for laser cutting machines, aiming to achieve high accuracy in cutting optical films. The method seeks to improve parameter tuning compared to traditional trial-and-error approaches.

items.title: HexEval: An Evidence-Driven Hexagonal Framework for Multidimensional Scholar Assessment
items.summary: HexEval introduces an evidence-driven hexagonal framework for multidimensional scholar assessment, leveraging LLM-based approaches. This method aims to provide a more comprehensive evaluation than traditional bibliometric indicators and reputation proxies.

items.title: FITTER: Vocabulary-Agnostic Cross-Domain Inference on Temporal Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: FITTER introduces a vocabulary-agnostic method for cross-domain inference on temporal knowledge graphs. This approach allows models to reason about entities, relations, and timestamps even when they are unknown at training time.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Deep Randomized Neural Networks for Classification
items.summary: This research introduces uncertainty-aware ensemble deep randomized neural networks for classification. This approach aims to improve robustness and effectiveness by addressing limitations in how current models handle diverse training samples.

items.title: Sheaf-Based Federated Representation Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes Sheaf-based Federated Representation Learning for heterogeneous federated systems. This method enables agents to learn and exchange informative representations despite differences in data distributions, sensing modalities, and model architectures.

items.title: Finding the Signal in the Spam: Jointly Learning Rewards and Worker Reliability from Pairwise Comparisons
items.summary: This research proposes a method for jointly learning item rewards and worker reliability from pairwise comparisons, which has applications in various domains, including fine-tuning large language models. The problem has been studied in recommendation systems and social choice.

items.title: Detecting Soft Skills in ML Engineering Roles CVs
items.summary: This paper explores methods for detecting soft skills in CVs for Machine Learning Engineering roles, aiming to understand candidate supply characteristics beyond what employers demand. It contributes to understanding collaboration needs among ML engineers, data scientists, and software engineers.

items.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Prognostics and Health Management: A Systematic Literature Review
items.summary: This is a systematic literature review on Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) within Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), highlighting how PIML addresses limitations of purely data-driven models in industrial reliability and safety. It examines advancements and challenges in the field.

items.title: Observational Policy Ranking for SMB Financial Guidance from Multi-Action Accounting Logs
items.summary: This research proposes an observational policy ranking framework to provide timely financial guidance to small and medium-sized businesses by analyzing multi-action accounting logs. It addresses the challenge of causal inference from self-selected business changes.

items.title: ChronoSSM: Training for Temporally Aware Representations in Autoregressive State Space Models
items.summary: This paper introduces ChronoSSM, a training methodology for autoregressive State Space Models to learn temporally aware representations. It aims to improve generative modeling by accounting for the 'when' of events, not just the 'what'.

items.title: SeFoRA: Sketch-Aggregated Federated Low-Rank Adaptation with Heterogeneous Client Ranks
items.summary: This paper introduces SeFoRA, a method for federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks using sketch-aggregated Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). It addresses the challenge of heterogeneous LoRA ranks among clients in federated learning.

items.title: REATS: LLM Reasoning-based Ensemble Learning for Adaptive Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: This paper introduces REATS, an LLM reasoning-based ensemble learning approach for adaptive time series forecasting, which leverages LLMs to dynamically select and combine forecasting models. It aims to overcome the limitations of single models across diverse real-world time series.

items.title: From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation
items.summary: This paper proposes a causal optimization framework for large-scale targeting and recommendation systems, shifting focus from predictive scores to maximizing incremental impact in applications like marketing campaigns. It aims to improve resource allocation by considering actual business goals.

items.title: Boundary-Seeking Policy Gradient for Safe Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces the Boundary-Seeking Policy Gradient method for safe reinforcement learning, which aims to maximize reward subject to safety constraints by ensuring the optimal policy lies on the constraint boundary. It addresses challenges in constrained Markov Decision Processes.

items.title: A matched-integrator evaluation of Hamiltonian neural networks on pendulum and Kepler dynamics
items.summary: This research provides a matched-integrator evaluation of Hamiltonian Neural Networks (HNNs) against parameter-matched feedforward neural networks for modeling conservative dynamics. It assesses the architectural prior benefit of HNNs on systems like pendulums and Kepler dynamics.

items.title: STCAD: Scalable Trajectory Clustering and Anomaly Detection on Terabyte-Scale AIS Data
items.summary: This paper introduces STCAD, a scalable framework for unsupervised clustering and anomaly detection of maritime trajectories from terabyte-scale AIS data. It uses a custom BERT-based model to encode variable-length trajectories.

items.title: CRHT: A Continuous Regression Hybrid Transformer for Vessel Trajectory Prediction with Online Cluster Sampling
items.summary: This paper proposes the Continuous Regression Hybrid Transformer (CRHT), a deep learning framework for accurate vessel trajectory prediction that addresses geographic bias and navigational realism using online cluster sampling. It aims to improve maritime safety and anomaly detection.

items.title: Accelerated Learning of High Dimensional Functions with a Tensor-Featured Training Network
items.summary: This paper presents a method using contextual features in the first layer of a deep neural network to accelerate the optimization of learning high-dimensional functions.

items.title: Fisher8: Stabilizing Neural Heteroscedastic Regression via Output-Layer Fisher Geometry
items.summary: This paper proposes Fisher8, a method to stabilize neural heteroscedastic regression by aligning gradient steps with the output-layer Fisher geometry.

items.title: Generator-Guided Inverse Sampling for L\'evy-Driven Generative Models
items.summary: This paper investigates inverse sampling for Lévy-driven generative models from the perspective of Markov generators, focusing on their non-local reverse processes.

items.title: Dreamer-SAC: Off-Policy Learning in Latent World Models for Sample-Efficient Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This work introduces Dreamer-SAC, an off-policy reinforcement learning approach in latent world models to achieve sample-efficient policy optimization for autonomous driving.

items.title: Share First, Route What Remains: A Unified Framework for Token-Adaptive MoE Computation
items.summary: This paper proposes a unified framework for token-adaptive Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) computation, combining shared-expert designs, fine-grained computation, and dynamic routing.

items.title: ELVAE: Evidential Learning-Based Variational Autoencoder for Uncertainty-Aware Generation
items.summary: This paper formulates ELVAE, an evidential learning-based Variational Autoencoder designed for uncertainty-aware generation that distinguishes between latent location uncertainty and variability.

items.title: Do Time-Series Forecasters Use the Right History: Recoverability, Recovery, and Functional Use of Temporal Delays
items.summary: This paper analyzes how time-series models use historical data, examining the recoverability of true delays, model reporting of delays, and their functional use in forecasting.

items.title: Critic-Free Pretraining for Efficient Online Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This paper proposes critic-free pretraining to enable more efficient online fine-tuning in offline-to-online reinforcement learning by avoiding issues with static, pre-trained critics.

items.title: Exploration-Driven Personalized Federated Reinforcement Learning via Intrinsic Motivation
items.summary: This paper presents a method for Personalized Federated Reinforcement Learning that uses exploration-driven intrinsic motivation to improve decentralized policy learning while maintaining client data privacy.

items.title: Retrieval-Corrected Conformal Prediction for Time Series
items.summary: This paper introduces retrieval-corrected conformal prediction, a method to provide more efficient and robust prediction intervals for time series data by adapting to changing forecast errors.

items.title: BREAD: Baseline-Referenced Explanations for Anomaly Diagnosis
items.summary: This paper introduces BREAD, a method for generating baseline-referenced explanations to diagnose anomalies detected by AI-based statistical process monitoring systems in high-dimensional settings.

items.title: $\beta$-VAEs as Effective Theories: Tolerance-Dependent Dimension
items.summary: This paper analyzes $\beta$-VAEs, showing how increased regularization strength acts as a spectral cutoff by collapsing low-utility latent coordinates and exploring its dependence on reconstruction utility.

items.title: Compute-Optimal Is Not Cluster-Optimal: Systems-Aware Scaling for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
items.summary: This paper argues for systems-aware scaling for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts models in large-scale pretraining, optimizing implementation across algorithm, architecture, and system decisions for cluster efficiency.

items.title: Pair-Centric Graph Rewiring for Over-Squashing via Optimal Transport-Guided Communication Alignment
items.summary: This paper proposes pair-centric graph rewiring, guided by optimal transport, to address the over-squashing problem in Message-Passing Neural Networks by improving communication alignment across distant graph regions.

items.title: ProbGuard: Calibrated Safety Risk Estimation from LLM Output Distributions
items.summary: This paper introduces ProbGuard, a method for calibrated safety risk estimation from Large Language Model output distributions, moving beyond deterministic classification for identifying unsafe LLM outputs.

items.title: IADD-TR: Intervention-Aware Dynamics Decoupling with Targeted Regularization for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces a method called IADD-TR for model-based reinforcement learning, aiming to improve dynamics prediction and policy optimization through intervention-aware dynamics decoupling and targeted regularization. It addresses challenges in sample-efficient decision-making.

items.title: Optimize Cheap, Deploy Strong: Cost-Aware Cross-Tier Transfer for Evolutionary Optimization
items.summary: This paper proposes a cost-aware cross-tier transfer method for the evolutionary optimization of LLM prompts and agentic programs. It aims to reduce the total search cost by restructuring the fitness evaluation process.

items.title: Your LLM, Your Style: Behavioral Mode Axes for LLM Behavioral Control
items.summary: This research investigates behavioral mode axes for controlling large language models' styles in interactive settings. It aims to improve understanding of how LLM behavioral styles affect user experience, safety, and decision-making.

items.title: Path Integral Value Matching for Linear Quadratic Stochastic Optimal Control
items.summary: This paper presents a Path Integral Value Matching method for Linear Quadratic Stochastic Optimal Control. It aims to address the prohibitive computational costs typically associated with current state-of-the-art policy-based methods in this framework.

items.title: MoE Proxy Models for Low-Cost Failure Reproduction and Diagnosis in LLM RL Post-Training
items.summary: This paper introduces MoE Proxy Models to enable low-cost failure reproduction and diagnosis in the computationally intensive reinforcement learning post-training of large language models. It aims to simplify debugging and address complexities arising from system pipelines and numerical issues.

items.title: TACTICL: Task-Aware Compression of Tabular ICL Models
items.summary: This paper introduces TACTICL, an automated task-aware compression method for tabular in-context learning models. It aims to reduce inference costs and computational demands by distilling models into more efficient, task-specific architectures.

items.title: Carefully Considering Culture: Analyzing LLM Alignment in Single- and Multi-Cultural Settings using Cultural Consensus Theory
items.summary: This research analyzes large language model alignment in single- and multi-cultural settings using Cultural Consensus Theory. It investigates LLM understanding of cultural norms, considering group consensus and diverse cultural environments.

items.title: The Multilingual Quantization Tax: Structural Collapse and Typological Fragility in Edge SLMs
items.summary: This paper examines the "multilingual quantization tax," which refers to the performance degradation and structural collapse observed when deploying 4-bit quantized Small Language Models (SLMs) on edge devices. It highlights the typological fragility of SLMs under quantization in multilingual contexts.

items.title: When Chain-of-Thought Helps and When It Hurts: An Empirical Investigation of the Serial-Depth Bottleneck in LLM Reasoning
items.summary: This empirical investigation explores when Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting benefits or harms large language model reasoning, specifically focusing on the serial-depth bottleneck. It examines the widely assumed universal improvement of CoT prompting.

items.title: Position Encoding in Transformers: From Absolute and Relative Methods to Rotary Position Embeddings and Long-Context Scaling
items.summary: This paper provides an overview of position encoding in Transformer models, covering methods from absolute and relative approaches to Rotary Position Embeddings. It discusses how position encoding addresses the lack of token order information in self-attention models and its relevance for long-context scaling.

items.title: PERCEPT: A Corpus for POS Tagging and Analysis of Persian-English Code-Mixing
items.summary: This paper introduces PERCEPT, a new corpus specifically developed for Part-of-Speech tagging and analysis of Persian-English code-mixing in social media. It aims to address the underexplored area of Persian-English code-mixed data in multilingual communication.

items.title: The Parser Already Knows: Lightweight Bias Correction in Constrained Decoding
items.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight bias correction method for Grammar Constrained Decoding (GCD) in language models. It aims to mitigate the distortion of a model's probability distribution when masking non-conforming tokens, which can lead to suboptimal outputs.

items.title: Multimodal Item Parameter Estimation using Simulated Response Probabilitie
items.summary: This research presents results on reconstructing multiple-choice model and three-parameter logistic model curves using a fine-tuned multimodal large language model based on Qwen3.5. The LLM is prompted and fine-tuned to replicate choice probabilities from a large training corpus.

items.title: Off-Axis, On Purpose: Where a Transformer Computes Concepts and Why it Does So
items.summary: This research investigates how Transformers compute concepts, focusing on the functional role of off-axis intermediate states rather than just the final unembedded answer. It reveals that a 12-layer model computes in two distinct phases.

items.title: Locally Deployable Small Language Models for Emergency Department Decision Support: A Systematic Benchmark of Fine-Tuning Strategies
items.summary: This research systematically benchmarks fine-tuning strategies for locally deployable small language models intended for emergency department decision support. It addresses challenges like privacy risks and the need for robust evaluation of open-source models in sensitive environments.

items.title: Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension
items.summary: This research paper investigates how minor architectural choices within transformer models significantly impact their accuracy and performance in long context settings.

items.title: MD-ProTector: Positioning Multiple Data-Driven Prototypes for LLM-Generated Text Detection
items.summary: This paper introduces MD-ProTector, a new system that uses multiple data-driven prototypes to detect LLM-generated text across diverse writing styles, domains, and languages.

items.title: Calibrating Post-Training Feature Shifts for LLM Data Contamination Detection
items.summary: This research proposes methods for detecting data contamination in Large Language Models by calibrating post-training feature shifts to determine if specific text was part of the pre-training corpus.

items.title: Simplex Relaxation for Discrete Diffusion
items.summary: This research explores uniform discrete diffusion models, investigating their corruption kernel and reverse prediction problem, and proposing simplex relaxation to enrich their training objective.

items.summary: This research identifies that decompose-then-verify fact-checking pipelines can introduce context-memory conflicts, causing them to contradict their own source text due to the decomposition process.

items.summary: This research proposes a method for auditing Chinese web-scale corpora using sampled BPE token statistics to identify pollution at a fine-grained level, addressing challenges of scale and analysis.

items.summary: This research investigates whether released Large Language Model vocabularies can be used to estimate token-level composition and corpus ratios of their hidden pretraining corpora.

items.title: EVIL-Detect for NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 6: LLM-Generated Text Detection
items.summary: This paper presents EVIL-Detect, a multi-signature system for detecting LLM-generated text in realistic Chinese scenarios, developed for the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 6.

items.title: Most biomedical publications show signs of LLM-assisted writing
items.summary: This study reports that most biomedical publications show evidence of Large Language Model-assisted writing, highlighting a widespread use with potential implications for academic integrity.

items.summary: This study explores reference-free post-training for multilingual machine translation using open large language models, applying Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tuned models like MiLMMT-46-v0.1.

items.title: X2-Turn: Frame-Synchronous Dual-Head Modeling for Joint Streaming ASR and Turn State Prediction

items.summary: This paper presents REAP, a system for constructing knowledge bases from large language models in a closed-book setting, using structured chain-of-thought reasoning and relation-specific query strategies.

items.summary: This introduces MUSE (Mining Underlying Scientific Explanations), a new full-text, cross-domain knowledge base that extracts scientific problems, solutions, and their rationales from research papers.

items.summary: P3CA (position-prompted PCA) is an encoder-agnostic method proposed for interpreting high-dimensional spatial embeddings of vision foundation models, particularly useful in medical image computing to inspect beyond task performance.

items.summary: MAD-HOI introduces a Masked Autoregressive Diffusion method for generating articulated hand-object interaction sequences from text, supporting features like variable-length generation and motion completion for more utilitarian outputs.

items.summary: This research focuses on Motion Artifact-Aware Self-Supervised Representation Learning to reduce motion artifacts in 3D Brain MRI, addressing image degradation caused by patient movement in quantitative analysis.

items.summary: DoseBridge is a denoising diffusion bridge model developed for accurate dose prediction in Lung Intensity-Modulated Proton Therapy, improving upon existing models by integrating beam geometry despite small clinical datasets.

items.summary: This research investigates whether vision models employ Gestalt grouping principles to organize visual content similarly to human vision, examining how they perceive wholes from parts.

items.summary: This paper proposes a Convolutional Layer Activation Dimensionality Reduction method for detecting out-of-distribution and adversarial attack samples, addressing trustworthiness and safety concerns in convolutional neural networks.

items.summary: Chain of Spatial Thoughts explores Modality-Agnostic Spatial Grounding for Vision Language Models, a fundamental capability for embodied intelligence applications such as robotic manipulation and autonomous driving.

items.summary: TRACE-GS presents an on-policy trajectory distillation framework that uses privileged geometric conditioning to adapt a diffusion prior for sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) restoration.

items.summary: SeFaR introduces a Semantic Feature-aware Robustness Testing method for Deep Neural Networks, aiming to evaluate perception models for reliability in safety-critical domains where failures can arise from rare scenarios.

items.summary: MRIComp4Flow focuses on the compression of 3D Brain MRI data to facilitate the training of large-scale multi-modal generative models, addressing challenges related to storage and I/O costs.

items.summary: UniMod is a method for enhancing multi-modal medical diagnosis by addressing shortcut learning through cross-modality and within-modality alignment, ensuring models effectively utilize both image and text data.

items.summary: This paper proposes ENCORE, an efficient noise context-aware representation model designed for low-dose CT denoising, which addresses limitations of conventional models by accounting for non-stationary and spatially correlated CT noise.

items.summary: This paper introduces CasDeblurGS, a method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that uses cascaded 2D-to-3D multi-view consistency to reconstruct 3D scenes from two blurry images, aiming to improve practical capture in immersive applications.
