items.title: AISafety.com Hackathon 2026
items.summary: A four-day, in-person hackathon to improve the AI safety resource hub. When Thursday 17th September – Sunday 20th September 2026 Where CEEALAR (the EA Hotel) in Blackpool, England Cost Free, including accommodation and all meals Applications close 14 August 2026 (decisions by 21 August) Once a year, the core AISafety.com team gets together with a group of amazing volunteers and spends an extended weekend getting a bunch of stuff done to improve the site. We also do some relaxed fun activities between work sessions. Who we're looking for Product managers and designers To execute the vision for new projects, build out design mockups, conduct user research, offer consulting, and brainstorm product solutions Project managers To lead and organize project efforts and run sprints Developers To work with product managers, designers, and AI tools to bring some amazing new things to life Connectors, people with an audience, and subject-matter experts To help us with targeted community outreach, general outreach, social media, and to give takes to product managers and designers Promotion people To help us spread awareness of the site and each resource page in various ways, maybe including SEO Anything else Just tell us how you can help! On the first day of the hackathon we will divide everyone into small teams by project . Participants will get to decide which projects they work on and in what way they contribute. We're also open to new project suggestions. Why it's worth it Build your resume, gain career capital, and make connections (everyone at the EA hotel, beyond just our hackathon, is working on something high-impact – mostly AI safety) Have fun beyond just the work. We'll set aside time each day for beach walks, games, etc. Help save the world! If you have any questions, please message Bryce on the AISafety.com Discord server at @bryceerobertson, or email bryceerobertson@gmail.com . Discuss

items.title: Shares in Chinese AI darlings slide on US ban fears
items.summary: Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink hit by report that Washington is drafting ban on optical transceivers

items.title: Beyond the Hivemind: Escaping LLM Homogeneity via Meta-Persona Anchoring and Sequential Temperature Scaling
items.summary: This paper identifies an 'Artificial Hivemind' effect in Large Language Models (LLMs) causing homogenized responses and proposes 'Meta-Persona Anchoring and Sequential Temperature Scaling' as a method to increase response diversity.

items.title: Towards a new paradigm of scientific discovery with socialized artificial intelligence
items.summary: This article discusses a conceptual shift towards a new paradigm of scientific discovery enabled by 'socialized artificial intelligence,' focusing on AI's role in organizing knowledge and extending inquiry.

items.title: When Compression Scores Cannot Decide: Information Boundaries for Group-Robust LLM Pruning
items.summary: This paper investigates why reproducible compression scores can fail to select optimal candidates for LLM pruning and proposes modeling the gap through information interfaces.

items.title: On the missing data layer and a potential solution
items.summary: This paper identifies the absence of a foundational 'dataset layer' as a critical problem for AI infrastructure in Latin America, proposing solutions for data discovery and supply.

items.title: Neurosymbolic Reasoning with Incremental Knowledge for Sample Efficient Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes using 'Neurosymbolic Reasoning with Incremental Knowledge' to improve sample efficiency in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) for tasks requiring long-horizon reasoning.

items.title: On the missing benchmarks layer and a potential solution
items.summary: This paper highlights the absence of a 'benchmark layer' in Latin American AI development, discussing its importance for auditing AI systems against regional requirements and directing optimization.

items.title: LoCA: Forward-Only LLM Tuning after One-Shot Calibration with Local Credit Assignment
items.summary: This paper proposes 'LoCA,' a novel 'Forward-Only LLM Tuning' method that enables parameter-efficient post-training after one-shot calibration, reducing the need for repeated backpropagation.

items.title: Evaluating Counterfactual Sensitivity to Patient Information in Medication-Safety Reasoning
items.summary: This study focuses on 'Evaluating Counterfactual Sensitivity' in AI models for 'Medication-Safety Reasoning' to ensure they apply patient-specific conditions correctly rather than merely recalling drug-risk associations.

items.title: AI Agent Economics: Can Autonomous Economic Behavior Emerge among AI Agents under Minimal External Conditions?
items.summary: This research explores 'AI Agent Economics' by investigating whether autonomous economic behavior can spontaneously emerge among AI agents under minimal external conditions, rather than being predefined.

items.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR
items.summary: This paper introduces Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization (OM-GRPO), a label-free reinforcement learning method to improve LLM reasoning by replacing ground-truth supervision with answer-level consensus.

items.title: Beyond Average Performance: Dynamic Instance Clustering and Specialized Algorithm Design in LLM-Assisted Evolutionary Search
items.summary: This research proposes dynamic instance clustering and specialized algorithm design within LLM-assisted evolutionary search to improve automated algorithm design beyond average performance optimization.

items.title: Spatial proteomics guided by H&E-based AI reveals recurrence-risk niches in triple-negative breast cancer
items.summary: This study developed an AI-guided spatial pathology framework that integrates deep learning models with spatial proteomics to identify recurrence-risk niches in triple-negative breast cancer.

items.title: UniGD: A Unified Generative-Discriminative Framework for Industrial Retrieval
items.summary: This paper introduces UniGD, a unified generative-discriminative framework designed for industrial retrieval in search advertising to meet strict relevance and latency requirements.

items.title: Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Knowledge Graph Construction for Multi-Lecture Educational Reasoning
items.summary: This paper presents an evidence-grounded multimodal pipeline for constructing knowledge graphs from lecture videos, integrating speech, slide text, diagrams, and equations.

items.title: Adversarial Stress Testing of Role-Playing Language Agents using Multi-Agent Evaluation
items.summary: This research focuses on adversarial stress testing and multi-agent evaluation techniques for Role-Playing Language Agents (RPLAs) in high-stakes applications. It aims to assess agent consistency and ethical constraints.

items.title: TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning
items.summary: This paper introduces TaskPress, a method for query-agnostic KV cache compression that uses task-guided pruning to optimize long-context inference in large language models.

items.title: AgentPanel: Toward a New Paradigm for Human--AI Collaboration in Exploring Scientific Questions
items.summary: This paper proposes AgentPanel, a new paradigm for human-AI collaboration aimed at exploring scientific questions by leveraging multiple AI perspectives. It addresses limitations of current human-AI interaction in research.

items.title: DocTrace: Towards Traceable Long Document VQA via Hierarchical Evidence Graph Reasoning
items.summary: This paper introduces DocTrace, a method for traceable long document Visual Question Answering (VQA) using hierarchical evidence graph reasoning with Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).

items.title: State Propagation Also Satisfies: A Complex-Valued State-Space Model for Deterministic State Tracking
items.summary: This paper proposes a complex-valued state-space model for deterministic state tracking tasks, offering an alternative to transformer-based architectures for sequence modeling. It suggests this new method may be more efficient for specific tasks like parity checking and modular counting.

items.title: Solver-Aware Decompositions for Programming-by-Example: When Dividing Requires Knowing how to Conquer
items.summary: This paper introduces a solver-aware decomposition approach for Programming-by-Example (PBE), where a learned decomposer predicts intermediate subgoals for a synthesizer. This method aims to improve performance by efficiently splitting complex tasks into manageable subtasks.

items.title: When Correct Solutions Repeat: Rarity-Aware Credit Redistribution for GRPO
items.summary: This paper introduces a rarity-aware credit redistribution method for GRPO in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). It addresses the issue of completion-level uniformity in GRPO, which can lead to skewed credit assignment for recurring correct solution forms.

items.title: Deep Divide-and-Reduce in Symbolic Regression
items.summary: This paper introduces a 'Deep Divide-and-Reduce' approach for symbolic regression (SR), aiming to discover underlying patterns in data and represent them mathematically. It seeks to improve machine learning methods for SR by incorporating a deeper understanding of mathematical and physical principles.

items.title: Multimodal Auto-regressive Transformer Surrogate for Modeling Variable Operations and Quantifying Uncertainty in Geological Carbon Storage
items.summary: This research develops a new multimodal auto-regressive transformer surrogate model to simulate variable operations and quantify uncertainty in geological carbon storage. The model aims to improve the efficiency of carbon storage by analyzing well perforation and injection strategies under geological uncertainty.

items.title: LLMs Can Annotate Attribution Graphs
items.summary: This paper proposes a pipeline that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the annotation of attribution graphs, a crucial step in circuit tracing for understanding internal language model computations. This method aims to simplify the previously manual and time-intensive process of grouping features into supernodes.

items.title: GeoID-PINN: Identifiability-Aware Regional Epidemic Inference with Geographic Coupling
items.summary: This paper introduces GeoID-PINN, an identifiability-aware physics-informed neural network for regional epidemic inference, specifically for SIRD (susceptible-infectious-recovered-deceased) dynamics. The model accounts for geographic coupling to better distinguish factors like local transmission and external infection pressure from surveillance data.

items.title: Verifier-Guided Model Discovery for Physical Dynamical Systems with Pretrained Symbolic Transformers
items.summary: This research proposes a verifier-guided model discovery approach for physical dynamical systems, leveraging pretrained symbolic transformers. The method aims to provide reliable forecasting for nonlinear physical systems, addressing the cost of high-fidelity simulations and the opacity of traditional machine-learning surrogates.

items.title: CT-HEG: A Bidirectional, Timestamp-Attributed Event Graph for ICU In-Hospital Mortality Prediction - An Architectural Ablation Study
items.summary: This paper introduces CT-HEG, a bidirectional, timestamp-attributed event graph model designed for accurate ICU in-hospital mortality prediction. It addresses limitations of existing models by effectively handling irregular clinical observations and heterogeneous entity types.

items.title: Sphere Retraction Normalizations
items.summary: This paper introduces Sphere Retraction Normalizations, a novel method for training deep neural networks stably, building upon Geodesic Normalization (GeoNorm). It recasts residual connections on a Riemannian manifold, orthogonalizing layer outputs and applying updates via a Riemannian exponential map.

items.title: Learning Molecular Representations from Cellular Phenotypes with Structure Preservation
items.summary: This research proposes a method for learning molecular representations from cellular phenotypes with structure preservation, addressing a gap in existing multimodal representation learning. It aims to better capture functional relationships in phenotypic drug discovery by considering the intrinsic organization of chemical space.

items.title: GLOBE: Trajectory-Aligned Gradient Matching with Structured SparseOptimization for Coreset Selection
items.summary: This paper introduces GLOBE, a method utilizing trajectory-aligned gradient matching with structured sparse optimization for coreset selection in deep neural network training. It aims to reduce computational and memory costs for on-device training by efficiently retaining a compact subset of training samples.

items.title: PatTree: a novel approach for automated creation of multimodal, graph-based patient representations for medical classification tasks
items.summary: This paper introduces PatTree, a novel approach for automatically creating multimodal, graph-based patient representations to enhance AI performance in medical classification tasks. It addresses the challenges of integrating heterogeneous and complex clinical real-world data for holistic patient understanding.

items.title: Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs for Efficient Options Pricing Models
items.summary: This paper applies Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs (NNLCI) to enhance the efficiency of numerical methods for pricing multi-asset options. It introduces a concise input format for NNLCI for substantial convenience and efficiency.

items.title: Evaluation Blindness: How Silent Measurement Failures Corrupt AI Systems from Training to Deployment
items.summary: This paper introduces "evaluation blindness," a phenomenon where silent measurement failures corrupt AI systems from training to deployment, leading to unnoticed propagation of errors. It highlights how these failures can lead to downstream harm before becoming visible.

items.title: Topological Simplification in Predictive Coding Networks
items.summary: This research investigates the topology of learned representations in predictive coding networks (PCNs), a neuro-inspired architecture, using quantitative layer-wise persistent homology analysis. The study trains PCNs on synthetic classification datasets.

items.title: Wiring Beats Blending: What Transfers Between Transformer Sizes -- and What Doesn't
items.summary: This study explores knowledge transfer between different sizes of Transformer models, specifically converting a 1.4B Pythia model to a 410M sibling. It characterizes how representations align strongly across sizes while parameters align weakly.

items.title: NOMADD: Numerical Optimization of Models Adapting to Data Drift
items.summary: This paper introduces NOMADD (Numerical Optimization of Models Adapting to Data Drift), a method designed to mitigate performance degradation in tabular models due to data drift and concept drift. It addresses changes in feature distributions or relationships over time.

items.title: Contrast-invariant deep ptychography neural networks
items.summary: This research addresses scaling inconsistencies in ptychography neural networks when generalizing out of distribution by introducing a factorization strategy. This method decouples learned object texture from measurement scaling, improving real-world viability.

items.title: GoT-CD: Graph-of-Thoughts Causal Discovery and the Fragility of Post-hoc Path-Specific Fairness Audits
items.summary: This research introduces GoT-CD (Graph-of-Thoughts Causal Discovery), a method for recovering directed structure from observational data. It explores its use in clinical settings for mechanism reasoning and discusses the fragility of post-hoc path-specific fairness audits.

items.title: Robust Counterfactual Policy Optimisation via Nondeterministic Causal Models
items.summary: This paper proposes a method for robust counterfactual policy optimization that utilizes nondeterministic causal models, addressing the limitations of traditional deterministic assumptions in sequential decision-making. It formalizes counterfactual policy optimization under these conditions.

items.title: Bayesian Data Reweighting Improves Multimodal Retrieval for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
items.summary: This research proposes using Bayesian data reweighting to improve multimodal retrieval systems for knowledge-based visual question answering. It aims to enhance the retrieval of external evidence for image-question pairs by addressing how unmatched query-document pairs are treated.

items.title: Federated generative event models for tokenized electronic health records
items.summary: This research evaluates federated training of tokenized generative event models (GEMs) across electronic health records from multiple institutions. It addresses limitations of siloed data and performance degradation in cross-site transfer for healthcare foundation models.

items.title: Sedentary Behavior Classification for Wearable Sensors with a CNN-BiLSTM Model
items.summary: This study uses a CNN-BiLSTM model to classify sedentary behavior from wearable sensor data, focusing on improving posture-based classification. It investigates the transferability of models trained on hip-worn data to wrist-worn accelerometers.

items.title: ATFlash: Per-RoPE-Wavelength Attention Windows for Compute/Memory-Efficient LLM Inference
items.summary: This paper introduces ATFlash, a method for compute/memory-efficient LLM inference using per-RoPE-wavelength attention windows. It optimizes attention scores by pruning query-key pairs based on rotary position embedding wavelength to improve efficiency.

items.title: Rubrics as Privileged Information for Open-Ended Generation
items.summary: This research extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by using rubrics as "privileged information" to improve open-ended generation models. It leverages structural constraints from ground-truth answers in verifiable domains like math.

items.title: Schedule-Informed Temporal Fusion Forecasting of Hourly Airport Security-Checkpoint Throughput
items.summary: This study develops a schedule-informed temporal fusion forecasting framework to predict hourly airport security-checkpoint throughput. It converts flight schedules into temporally aligned signals to more accurately forecast passenger arrival times for staffing needs.

items.title: SP3O: Reinforcement Learning from Segment Preferences without Reward Modeling
items.summary: This paper introduces SP3O, a new method for preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) in general stochastic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) that operates without requiring a reward model. It addresses limitations of existing reward-model-free techniques.

items.title: Inverted Detection and Control in Steering Vectors
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for detecting and controlling concepts in large language model outputs using inverted steering vectors. It challenges the assumption of linear discriminability in steering vectors.

items.title: Scaling an Autoregressive Transformer for Single-Cell Generation
items.summary: This research studies the application of a scaled autoregressive transformer for generating single-cell gene expression vectors. The paper characterizes the biological fidelity and performance of the generated data.

items.title: AcceptMoE: Commitment-Weighted Self-Sizing Verifier Expert Sets for Efficient MoE Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This research proposes AcceptMoE, a method using commitment-weighted self-sizing verifier expert sets for efficient speculative decoding in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. It aims to reduce unnecessary expert activations during parallel verification.

items.title: Joint Affine Spectral Shaping: Coupling Weight and Bias Updates Beyond Weight-Only Muon
items.summary: This paper introduces Joint Affine Spectral Shaping, an optimization method that couples weight and bias updates in neural networks. It formulates affine layers as a joint momentum matrix and applies spectral mapping.

items.title: A Graph Signal Processing Perspective on Numerical Sequence Representations in LLM In-Context Learning
items.summary: This research analyzes numerical sequence representations in LLM in-context learning through a graph signal processing perspective. It aims to better understand how LLMs perform numerical inference.

items.title: Paired Recipient-based Evaluation of Survival Prediction for Deceased Donor Kidney Transplants
items.summary: This research explores the use of machine learning for predicting kidney transplant outcomes and proposes a paired recipient-based evaluation method for these survival predictions. The goal is to improve donor-recipient matching.

items.title: PLAN: Parallel Liquid-Inspired Approximation Network for Efficient Representation Learning in Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
items.summary: This research introduces PLAN, a Parallel Liquid-Inspired Approximation Network, designed for efficient representation learning in flexible job shop scheduling using deep reinforcement learning. It aims to overcome limitations of attention-centric models.

items.title: SynEnergy: Anomaly Semantic-Guided Diffusion for Synthetic Energy Data Generation
items.summary: This research proposes SynEnergy, an anomaly semantic-guided diffusion model for generating synthetic fine-grained energy consumption data. The goal is to address privacy concerns and data-sharing constraints.

items.title: SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation
items.summary: This research introduces SMOPD, a method for multi-reward reinforcement learning that uses specialize-and-merge online policy distillation. It aims to improve model performance by addressing issues with reward signal interaction.

items.title: Convex-Hull-Neighborhood Smooth Dual Generalization: Controlling Local Correction Propagation in Offline RL
items.summary: This research introduces a method called Convex-Hull-Neighborhood Smooth Dual Generalization to control local correction propagation in offline reinforcement learning. It aims to manage estimation errors from out-of-distribution actions.

items.title: On the Implicit Flatness Bias of Sharpness-Aware Minimization: A Linear Stability Analysis with Quantitative Hyperparameter Bounds
items.summary: This research provides a linear stability analysis of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), clarifying its implicit bias toward flat minima. It also offers quantitative hyperparameter bounds for the perturbation radius.

items.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?
items.summary: Presents BODHI, a study investigating whether reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) genuinely expands the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) or primarily improves sampling efficiency.

items.title: Character Iconicity vs. Arbitrariness: An Arabic NLP Perspective
items.summary: Explores the functional necessity of visual distinctions in Arabic script through an Arabic NLP perspective, using dot removal experiments to analyze character iconicity versus arbitrariness.

items.title: Mapping the City Through the Lens of Language Models
items.summary: Explores how language models interpret underspecified references to cities, measuring their inherent assumptions about urban size, form, infrastructure, environment, and function.

items.title: TQLite: Multi-LLM Jury Guided Distillation for Real-time MQM Translation Quality Evaluation
items.summary: Presents TQLite, a multi-LLM jury guided distillation method for real-time MQM (Multidimensional Quality Metrics) translation quality evaluation, addressing the computational expense of large models.

items.title: Language Models Encode the Contextual Truth of Propositions
items.summary: This research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) encode contextual truth by maintaining linear representations of propositions, even when truth is derived from in-context evidence rather than world knowledge.

items.title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation
items.summary: This research explores the divergent strengths of base and post-trained Large Language Models (LLMs) in simulating human opinions, attributing conflicting prior results to the conflation of different model types.

items.title: SeqLLM: Augmenting LLMs with Behavioral-Sequence Modeling for High-Stakes Decisions at WeChat Pay
items.summary: SeqLLM augments Large Language Models (LLMs) with behavioral-sequence modeling to enhance merchant risk control at WeChat Pay, enabling more accurate high-stakes decisions by jointly understanding textual profiles and behavioral sequences.

items.title: Activation-Guided Neuron Intervention to Induce Alzheimer's-Related Computational Language Phenotypes in a Large Language Model
items.summary: Researchers introduce an activation-guided neuron intervention method to induce Alzheimer's-related computational language phenotypes in a Large Language Model (LLM), helping to establish if model representations functionally contribute to disease-related speech changes.

items.title: CVPO: Enhancing LLM Reinforcement Learning Reasoning via Value-Variance Adaptation and Dynamic Curriculum Learning
items.summary: CVPO is a new method that enhances Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning capabilities through reinforcement learning, utilizing value-variance adaptation and dynamic curriculum learning to address feedback precision and problem difficulty drift.

items.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation
items.summary: PAMT (Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning) is introduced to improve multi-domain machine translation, enabling large reasoning models to make domain-sensitive decisions such as disambiguation and terminology control.

items.title: Scalable Frequency- and Length-Aware Subdocument Deduplication for Large Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: This paper presents a scalable method for frequency- and length-aware subdocument deduplication in large-scale pretraining corpora, aiming to remove redundancy beyond document-level deduplication for Large Language Model training.

items.title: HomoEnsNER: Does Language Alignment Outperform Architectural Complexity in Gujarati Named Entity Recognition?
items.summary: HomoEnsNER investigates whether language alignment or architectural complexity is more effective for Named Entity Recognition (NER) in Gujarati, a language challenged by specific linguistic characteristics.

items.title: From SQL Errors to Concept Gaps: An AI-Powered Knowledge Graph Analytics Platform for Personalized Feedback
items.summary: This paper describes an AI-powered knowledge graph analytics platform that provides personalized feedback to students learning SQL by connecting their errors to conceptual gaps in database systems courses.

items.title: Internalizing Academic Writing Workflows for Introduction Generation via Struct-Aware Policy Learning
items.summary: This research proposes internalizing academic writing workflows for introduction generation using Large Language Models (LLMs) via Struct-Aware Policy Learning, aiming to improve coordination of background, gap, method, and contribution in coherent narratives.

items.title: Aligning Large Vision-Language Models at Test Time: A Trajectory-Guided Structured Sampling Approach
items.summary: This paper introduces a Trajectory-Guided Structured Sampling Approach for aligning Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) at test time, addressing resource-intensive training and mismatches found in existing RL-based alignment methods.

items.title: On the Diversity of Analogy Making in Large Language Models
items.summary: This research explores the diversity of analogy-making capabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs), investigating this core cognitive function that contributes to novelty and creativity.

items.title: FACTWASH: Catching AI Rewrites That Wash Hearsay into Fact
items.summary: Introduces "factwashing," a phenomenon where AI systems rewrite information, removing its verifiable source, and releases `factwash`, an open-source tool designed to detect such AI rewrites that turn hearsay into apparent fact.

items.title: Don't Let Me Ask for It: LLMs Show Deficiencies in Active Multi-Turn Information Acquisition for Abductive Inference
items.summary: A research paper investigating deficiencies in Large Language Models' (LLMs) active multi-turn information acquisition strategies when performing abductive inference, despite their ability to solve such reasoning tasks.

items.title: Predicting Multilingual Classification and Translation Performance of LLMs with Cross-Lingual Alignment $\unicode{x2013}$ Is English Enough?
items.summary: A study investigating whether English-aligned cross-lingual alignment (CLA) scores can predict the multilingual classification and translation performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in non-English tasks.

items.title: Probing Character-level Transformers for the Spanish L-shaped Morphome
items.summary: Research probing character-level transformers to understand how they learn complex irregular morphological patterns, using the Spanish L-shaped morphome as a test case.

items.title: ChronoLens: Measuring Language Change Across Time, Languages, and Linguistic Levels
items.summary: Introduces ChronoLens, a computational method for measuring historical language change across different linguistic levels and languages, addressing the challenge of incompatible representations in existing studies.

items.title: Consensus Measures for Unstructured Biomedical Text Annotations
items.summary: A study on improving consensus measures and soft inter-rater reliability for annotators working with open-ended labels in unstructured biomedical text annotations.

items.title: SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists: A Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Multi-Task Learning for LLMs
items.summary: A theoretical and empirical analysis comparing Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) for multi-task learning in Large Language Models (LLMs), revealing task conflicts in SFT during multi-stage training.

items.title: Looking under the Wrong Lamppost: On the Limitations of Automated Translation Quality Estimation
items.summary: A critical analysis of the limitations inherent in automated Translation Quality Estimation (QE) systems, discussing their shortcomings despite their growing adoption for managing translation quality at scale.

items.title: A Unified 2D Framework for DeepLesion Detection, Segmentation and Short Report Generation
items.summary: Develops a unified 2D framework for medical image analysis, integrating LLM-based reasoning for lesion detection, segmentation, and short report generation from the DeepLesion dataset.

items.title: In-Context Collapse in Vision-Language Models and How to Mitigate it?
items.summary: Identifies and analyzes "in-context collapse" in Vision-Language Models during many-shot in-context learning, where performance surprisingly degrades with more demonstrations, and proposes mitigation strategies.

items.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Deep Learning Framework for Color Reconstruction of Lenticular Films
items.summary: Proposes a human-in-the-loop deep learning framework for accurately reconstructing colors in historical lenticular films, which encode color information in a distinctive spatial format.

items.title: Test Time Adaptation Methods for Point Cloud Registration in Laparoscopic Surgery
items.summary: Investigates test time adaptation methods for 3D point cloud registration in laparoscopic surgery, which estimates organ transformations by adapting networks trained on synthetic data to real-time scenarios.

items.title: Clinically-Grounded Hierarchical Classification for Consistent Chest X-ray Interpretation
items.summary: Proposes a clinically-grounded hierarchical classification method to improve the consistency and accuracy of automated chest X-ray interpretation by structuring reasoning from broad anatomical systems to specific pathological findings.

items.title: Standalone DINOv3 for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing
items.summary: Explores the use of standalone DINOv3, specifically DINO.txt, for training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation in remote sensing, leveraging image-text contrastive learning to overcome annotation costs.

items.title: AIDE: Automated Instruction via Distilled Expertise for Reference-Free Motor Skill Coaching
items.summary: Proposes "AIDE" (Automated Instruction via Distilled Expertise), a reference-free method for generating natural-language coaching feedback on motor skills, aiming to accelerate learning without requiring expert demonstrations.

items.title: Bimanual Manipulation Within an 8 GB Budget: Zero-Copy Sensing and Quantized ACT on an Entry-Level Jetson
items.summary: Bimanual manipulation policies trained with imitation learning are typically evaluated on workstation or datacenter-class GPUs, leaving the cost of deploying them on embedded hardware largely uncharacterized. We present a bimanual SO-101 system running entirely on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super (8 GB), the entry-level tier of NVIDIA's embedded line, using a desktop GPU (RTX 3070) only for offline training, evaluated on pick-and-place of a deformable beanbag. First, we build a GStreamer capture pipeline backed by NVMM buffers that removes redundant host-device copies from three-camera sensing. Contrary to expectation, the conventional path fit the memory budget and dropped no frames; what zero-copy sensing recovers is CPU headroom (peak single-core utilization 98.0% to 77.0%) and worst-case latency (117.31 ms to 101.52 ms). Second, we train ACT and Diffusion Policy on identical demonstrations, each at its own reference budget (100k gradient steps for ACT, 200k for Diffusion Policy). ACT converges to a task-competent policy (19/20 trials) while Diffusion Policy does not converge to a usable one (0/10) even at twice the step count, which we attribute to differing convergence costs rather than an accuracy ceiling. Third, we convert ACT to TensorRT. FP16 reduces mean inference latency from 114.02 ms to 17.93 ms (6.4x) and INT8 to 12.65 ms (9.0x), with task success preserved at all three precisions (19/20, 18/20, 19/20). We report two findings not previously documented for ACT: TensorRT's general-purpose INT8 calibration quantizes the ResNet18 backbone but accepts zero of 145 transformer layers, explaining INT8's negligible size reduction over FP16 (0.9%) despite a further 28% latency gain; and the need for quantization is conditional on ACT's action-chunking configuration, feasible in full precision at n_action_steps = 100 but not at the per-step re-prediction temporal ensembling requires.

items.title: Stochastic Multiple Shooting Trajectory Optimization via Sequential Local Policy Evaluation
items.summary: Stochastic single shooting trajectory optimization methods such as Model Predictive Path Integral control (MPPI) have been widely adopted in robotics due to their ability to reason about probabilistic dynamics and provide solutions where model gradients are noisy, costly to evaluate, or unavailable. However, satisfaction of terminal constraints when shooting over long action sequences is often sample inefficient, requiring a large number of iterations for convergence. In this paper, we present a stochastic multiple shooting method that optimizes short control action sequences connected via local feedback policies to improve sample efficiency and convergence to a terminal set. Additionally, we show that we are able to synthesize approximate system Jacobians purely from rollouts, making the method suitable for model-based reinforcement learning with black-box dynamics. We demonstrate the algorithm has improved sample efficiency and terminal set convergence for three nonlinear, underactuated optimization problems: a classic cartpole swingup task with analytical dynamics, a cartpole swingup task with learned neural network dynamics, and a VTOL quadplane performing a high angle-of-attack, precision post-stall landing maneuver.

items.title: SLAMFormer-$\infty$: Infinite SLAM Transformer for Unbounded Frontend and Backend Processing
items.summary: We introduce the Infinite SLAM Transformer (SLAMFormer-$\infty$), the first geometric transformer capable of supporting both long-range frontend and backend processing without an explicit distance bound. Instead of relying on a first-frame-anchored formulation, SLAMFormer-$\infty$ employs memory conditions to define flexible coordinate systems and scales for input frames, enabling more expressive structural conditioning. Built upon this formulation, the frontend preserves efficient local computation, while the backend jointly optimizes long-range trajectories and scene geometry in a globally consistent manner. Experimental results demonstrate that SLAMFormer-$\infty$ achieves superior or highly competitive performance in both trajectory estimation and scene reconstruction across large-scale datasets. Notably, SLAMFormer-$\infty$ generalizes to extremely long trajectories, successfully operating on sequences exceeding $17\mathrm{km}$.

items.title: PhyAI: Real-Time Physical AI at the Edge, Scalable Rollouts in the Cloud
items.summary: Physical AI policies require inference throughout their lifecycle, including model evaluation, cloud reinforcement learning rollout, edge GPU serving, and onboard deployment. Although these settings share the same checkpoint and action semantics, they often rely on separate inference programs. To unify them, we build PhyAI, a Physical AI inference engine with a single runtime that keeps architecture-specific conditioning, solver, cache, and output logic in model adapters while sharing graph execution, kernels, memory management, and parallel services. The same codebase runs vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models (WAMs) on single or multiple GPUs across onboard, edge, and cloud deployments. We used the adapter interface to add MiniCPM-Robot on the day of its release. PhyAI achieves 1.40x-4.65x speedups over the official implementations of pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.7, and MiniCPM-Robot. On Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID it reduces latency from 2.46 to 1.18 s on eight H20 GPUs (CFG=2, TP=4), a 2.08x speedup. Specialized runtimes remain faster in several configurations, so our goal is one runtime with competitive latency rather than the fastest result in every case. Detailed profiles reveal why different models need different execution policies: on a Hopper-series GPU at batch size one, the pi0.5 action expert accounts for 8.8% of FLOPs but 57.2% of latency; at batch size 32 its share drops to 13.5% and throughput reaches about 100 samples/s. Cosmos3 remains generation-dominated and gains only 14.3% throughput as batch size increases from 1 to 16. We further introduce the control-time Roofline, which distinguishes inference-bound from environment-bound control; the measured pi0.5 points on four LIBERO suites are environment-bound while Cosmos3 stays inference-bound. Code and benchmarks: https://github.com/mingti-org/phyai.

items.title: Mixed-Initiative Human-Robot Teaming under Suboptimality with Online Bayesian Adaptation
items.summary: For effective human-agent teaming, robots and other artificial intelligence (AI) agents must infer their human partner's abilities and behavioral response patterns and adapt accordingly. Most prior works make the unrealistic assumption that one or more teammates can act near-optimally. In real-world collaboration, humans and autonomous agents can be suboptimal, especially when each only has partial domain knowledge. In this work, we develop computational modeling and optimization techniques for enhancing the performance of suboptimal human-agent teams, where the human and the agent have asymmetric capabilities and act suboptimally due to incomplete environmental knowledge. We adopt an online Bayesian approach that enables a robot to infer people's willingness to comply with its assistance in a sequential decision-making game. Our user studies show that user preferences and team performance indeed vary with robot intervention styles, and our approach for mixed-initiative collaborations enhances objective team performance ($p<.001$) and subjective measures, such as user's trust ($p<.001$) and willingness to comply with the robot ($p<.001$).

items.title: Electrostatic Clutch-Based Mechanical Multiplexer with Increased Force Capability
items.summary: As robotic systems become increasingly articulated, conventional actuation still dedicates one motor to each degree of freedom (DoF). Mechanical multiplexers address this limitation by allowing a single motor to control multiple outputs through clutches, reducing the number of required motors. However, previous multiplexers have relied on bulky mechanical clutch designs, limiting their development. This study presents an electrostatic capstan clutch-based transmission architecture that enables high-force mechanical multiplexing with independent, simultaneous, and fully actuated control of multiple outputs from a single motor. Our transmission implements four fully-actuated linear outputs, achieving individual output forces of up to 212 N and output speeds of up to 69.5 mm/s. We demonstrate our transmission on a commercial tendon-driven hand, where sequentially allocating system-wide torque capacity to individual outputs increased vertical grip strength by 4.09x and raised horizontal carrying capacity to 111.2 N, the highest reported among five-fingered tendon-driven robotic hands. These results demonstrate that electrostatic clutch-based mechanical multiplexing enables high-force, independent, simultaneous, and fully actuated control while overcoming the limitations of previous mechanical multiplexers.

items.title: FGGS-LiDAR: Ultra-Fast, GPU-Accelerated Simulation from General 3DGS Models to LiDAR
items.summary: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a strong representation for photorealistic rendering, its vast ecosystem of assets remains difficult to use for high-performance LiDAR simulation, a critical tool for robotics and autonomous driving. We present \textbf{FGGS-LiDAR}, a geometry-first framework that bridges this gap in a plug-and-play manner. Our method converts pretrained 3DGS assets into watertight meshes directly from Gaussian parameters, without requiring LiDAR-specific supervision or architectural alterations, via volumetric discretization and Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) extraction. We pair this with a GPU-accelerated ray-casting module that simulates LiDAR returns at over 500 FPS and supports batched multi-environment simulation with up to 4096 environments. In large-scale parallel settings, FGGS-LiDAR achieves an order-of-magnitude lower LiDAR simulation latency than Isaac Sim. We validate FGGS-LiDAR on both indoor and outdoor scenes, demonstrating high LiDAR-simulation fidelity. Furthermore, on COLMAP-posed indoor benchmarks, we compare against existing 3DGS-to-mesh baselines and report lower LiDAR-simulation error. Code is at https://github.com/discoverse-dev/FGGS-LiDAR.

items.title: PACE: Physics Augmentation for Coordinated End-to-end Reinforcement Learning toward Versatile Humanoid Table Tennis
items.summary: Humanoid table tennis (TT) demands rapid perception, proactive whole-body motion, and agile footwork under strict timing--capabilities that remain difficult for end-to-end control policies. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that maps ball-position observations directly to whole-body joint commands for both arm striking and leg locomotion, strengthened by predictive signals and dense, physics-guided rewards. A lightweight learned predictor, fed with recent ball positions, estimates future ball states and augments the policy's observations for proactive decision-making. During training, a physics-based predictor supplies precise future states to construct dense, informative rewards that lead to effective exploration. The resulting policy attains strong performance across varied serve ranges (hit rate$\geq$96% and success rate$\geq$92%) in simulations. Ablation studies confirm that both the learned predictor and the predictive reward design are critical for end-to-end learning. Deployed zero-shot on a physical Booster T1 humanoid with 23 revolute joints, the policy produces coordinated lateral and forward-backward footwork with accurate, fast returns, suggesting a practical path toward versatile, competitive humanoid TT. We have open-sourced our RL training code at: https://github.com/purdue-tracelab/TTRL-ICRA2026

items.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
items.summary: Explores optimizing cache reuse policies to reduce inference overhead in diffusion models, identifying current policies' mismatch with global efficiency.

items.title: LoKiFormer: Locality-aware Attention with Decoupled Knowledge Memory for Efficient Large Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: Introduces LoKiFormer, an architecture that uses locality-aware attention and decoupled knowledge memory to improve the efficiency of Large Language Model pretraining.

items.title: MAG: MAnifold Guided Semi-Supervised Multi-modal In-Context Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces MAG, a manifold-guided semi-supervised multi-modal in-context learning method to improve task adaptation for multi-modal large language models using both labeled and unlabeled data. It addresses the sensitivity of few-shot ICL to demonstration quality.

items.title: HiRoute: Hierarchical Routed Prompt Tuning for Safety Alignment of Large Language Models
items.summary: HiRoute introduces a hierarchical routed prompt tuning method to improve the safety alignment of Large Language Models, making them more robust against harmful requests and jailbreak attacks.

items.title: CardioState-JEPA: Delay-Aware Cross-Modal Learning of a Shared Cardiac Representation
items.summary: CardioState-JEPA introduces a delay-aware cross-modal learning approach to develop a shared cardiac representation from multi-sensor data (ECG, PPG, PCG), improving upon existing single-modality cardiac foundation models.

items.title: Balanced Adaptive Prototype Selection for Scalable TabPFN Inference on Large-Scale Tabular Data
items.summary: This paper introduces Balanced Adaptive Prototype Selection (BAPS), a framework designed to enable scalable inference for pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN) on large-scale tabular datasets.

items.title: Incremental Evaluation and Training in Relational Deep Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes methods for incremental evaluation and training in Relational Deep Learning models, which process multi-tabular databases as temporal heterogeneous graphs, to better reflect the continuous nature of real-world data.

items.title: FastThaiG2P: Lightning-fast Thai Grapheme-to-phoneme Conversion for Voice Agent Pipelines
items.summary: FastThaiG2P is a fast Thai grapheme-to-phoneme conversion model designed for text-to-speech pipelines, supporting International Phonetic Alphabet and Kokoro-TTS conventions. It uses a PyThaiNLP-tokenized, extensible dictionary and normalization rules for Central Thai speech.

items.title: Decoupled Contrastive Decoding via Expert-Aligned Drafting
items.summary: This paper introduces Decoupled Contrastive Decoding via Expert-Aligned Drafting, a method to improve generation quality and accelerate Contrastive Decoding by addressing the proposal-alignment question in speculative decoding.

items.title: Unifying Depth and Width Pruning for LLMs via Binary Knapsack Optimization
items.summary: This paper presents SNIPER, a two-stage structured pruning framework that unifies depth and width pruning for large language models using binary knapsack optimization. It aims to improve upon greedy heuristics for model compression.

items.title: CASA: Content-Acoustic Speaking Assessment with Speech Encoder and Large Language Model
items.summary: CASA is a Content-Acoustic Speaking Assessment system that uses a speech encoder and a large language model to evaluate speaking performance. It provides analysis of how acoustic and content information contribute to predictions in multimodal speech LLMs.

items.title: GEM: A Generative Embedding Model Bridging Reasoning and Retrieval
items.summary: GEM is a new Generative Embedding Model designed to bridge reasoning and retrieval for large language models, addressing the gap between how users express complex information needs and how conventional retrievers operate.

items.title: Mixture of Training: Recombining Small-Scale Scaffolded Pretraining Runs into a Larger Language Model
items.summary: This paper introduces Mixture of Training (MoT), a scaffolded modular pre-training procedure that allows language models to be trained by recombining smaller, independently trained jobs into a larger, coherent model.

items.title: HIMEC: Directional Change Representation and Fixed-Interface Decoding for Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning
items.summary: This research presents HIMEC, a method for remote sensing image change captioning that converts bitemporal imagery into sentences describing semantic changes by using directional change representation and fixed-interface decoding.

items.title: From Visual Widgets to UI Code: Efficient Tool-Grounded Generation
items.summary: This research explores efficient tool-grounded generation to improve screenshot-to-code systems, aiming to reduce hallucination in direct multimodal generation by using structured pipelines with component-wise decomposition and customized representations.

items.title: Mr3D-VL: A generalist vision language foundation model for Multiparametric 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging
items.summary: This paper introduces Mr3D-VL, a generalist vision-language foundation model designed for multiparametric 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging (mpMRI) to improve brain tumor diagnosis and treatment by enabling natural language interaction and interpretability.

items.title: VOS-Agent: The 1st Place Solution for the 8th LSVOS Challenge (MOSEv2 Track)
items.summary: This article describes VOS-Agent, the first-place solution for the 8th LSVOS Challenge (MOSEv2 Track), which addresses complex video object segmentation requiring robust target propagation under severe occlusion, disappearance, and reappearance.

items.title: Erase but Preserve: Controllable Removal of Copyrighted Animation Characters via Optimized Semantic Anchors
items.summary: This paper presents a method for controllable removal of copyrighted animation characters from text-to-image diffusion models using optimized semantic anchors, addressing copyright concerns related to unauthorized reproduction.

items.title: LocusGS: Spatially Grounded Tokens for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: This research introduces LocusGS, a method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that uses spatially grounded tokens and learnable queries to represent and decode 3D scenes more effectively.

items.title: Semantic Steering for Controllable Generation: Tuning-Free Concept Erasure in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: This paper presents a method for controllable generation in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) to enable tuning-free concept erasure and address safety concerns in text-to-image generation.

items.title: HounsWorld: A Multimodal World Model for Hidden Patient-State Readout, Reconstruction, and Simulation
items.summary: HounsWorld is presented as a multimodal world model designed for clinical intelligence, enabling the estimation of a patient's hidden state, reconstruction, and simulation from incomplete medical observations and language.

items.title: TennisVAR: A Stroke-Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Large Language Model for Tactical Reasoning in Tennis Videos
items.summary: TennisVAR is introduced as a stroke-evidence-grounded Multimodal Large Language Model developed for tactical reasoning in tennis videos, moving beyond individual stroke perception to explain match progression.

items.title: Spatially-Grounded Text-to-Video Generation via Inference-Time Gradient-Free Optimization
items.summary: This research focuses on achieving spatially-grounded text-to-video generation using Diffusion Transformer models, employing inference-time gradient-free optimization to improve fine-grained spatial controllability.

items.title: Paths: Prompt-aware Spatio-temporal Transformer with Hierarchical Multi-modal Fusion for RGB-Event Video Person Re-Identification
items.summary: Paths introduces a prompt-aware spatio-temporal Transformer with hierarchical multi-modal fusion for RGB-Event Video Person Re-Identification (RE-VReID), improving person tracking across non-overlapping cameras.

items.title: Towards Physics-Faithful Generation of Scientific Diagrams
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of current text-to-image models in generating scientifically accurate diagrams, focusing on the need for physical faithfulness over photorealistic quality. It highlights the unreliability of state-of-the-art systems for tasks requiring correct force directions or valid coordinate systems.

items.title: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: DreamX-Phi 1.0 is an action-conditioned video world model for robotic manipulation that predicts future observations given an initial frame, language instruction, and a prescribed sequence of end-effector poses and gripper states.

items.title: RadarGen: Automotive Radar Point Cloud Generation from Cameras
items.summary: This research introduces RadarGen, a diffusion model that synthesizes realistic automotive radar point clouds using multi-view camera imagery, adapting image-latent diffusion for the radar domain.

items.summary: CORA-Diff proposes a method to improve the efficiency of Diffusion Language Model inference by addressing fixed denoising horizons and optimizing blockwise decoding processes.

items.title: Click2Poly: A VLM for vector mapping buildings and walls
items.summary: This introduces Click2Poly, a Vision-Language Model (VLM) specifically designed for accurate vector mapping of buildings and walls for geospatial applications.

items.title: Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets
items.summary: This research explores retrofitting recurrent depth into a specific pretrained language model, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, to study its effects on installation, extrapolation, transfer, and retention. It aims to enhance the model's capabilities without increasing its size significantly.

items.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs
items.summary: This work proposes Self-Fix Step-DPO (SFS-DPO), a reinforcement learning framework designed to improve LLMs' ability to self-correct by enabling step-level self-verification and correction of their own mistakes.

items.title: Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing for Composable Unstructured Knowledge Editing
items.summary: This paper introduces Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing, a method for composable unstructured knowledge editing in LLMs. It aims to update specific knowledge within an LLM to prevent it from becoming outdated, without requiring full model retraining.

items.title: Ripple-Pivot Search: Active Parallel Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces Ripple-Pivot Search, an active parallel decoding method for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs). This technique aims to significantly speed up inference compared to autoregressive models by optimizing parallel decoding schedules.

items.title: AWARe: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting via Activation-Weighted Adaptive REtention
items.summary: AWARe is a proposed method aimed at mitigating catastrophic forgetting in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) during fine-tuning on downstream tasks. It uses Activation-Weighted Adaptive Retention to prevent the degradation of previously acquired knowledge.

items.title: Language-Conditional Dequantization: Recovering What Quantization Steals from Non-English Languages
items.summary: This work proposes Language-Conditional Dequantization (LCD), a post-hoc method to recover multilingual capabilities lost during aggressive quantization of LLMs. It addresses the disproportionate perplexity degradation observed in non-English languages compared to English.

items.title: TELLME: Test-Enhanced Learning for Language Model Enrichment
items.summary: This study proposes TELLME (Test-Enhanced Learning for Language Model Enrichment), a new method to improve continual pre-training (CPT) for domain adaptation in LLMs. It aims to address challenges associated with acquiring large datasets and high computational costs in CPT.

items.title: BoltNet: An Ultra-Lightweight Convolutional Network for On-Device Plant Species Identification
items.summary: Introduces BoltNet, an ultra-lightweight convolutional network designed for on-device plant species identification from citizen-science imagery, balancing capacity with memory, latency, and power constraints for field use.

items.title: HarmoniDPO: Video-guided Audio Generation via Preference-Optimized Diffusion
items.summary: Introduces HarmoniDPO, a method for video-guided audio generation that utilizes preference-optimized diffusion to achieve precise temporal synchronization and high perceptual quality, addressing challenges in the video-to-audio relationship.

items.title: G0.5: One Autoregressive Stream for Robot Reasoning and Action
items.summary: Introduces G0.5, a pretrained autoregressive Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that uses a single transformer decoder for robot reasoning and action, unifying the VLM's role as a decision-maker rather than just a context encoder.

items.summary: This paper introduces Power Law Graph Attention (PLGA), an exact generalization of scaled dot-product attention for Large Language Models, which replaces the fixed bilinear form with a learned, input-generated operator. It observes empirical collapse at inference.

items.title: ProTAGAD: A Foundation Model for TAG Anomaly Detection with Decoupled Topological and Textual Prototypes

items.title: FACT: Failure-Aware Causal Training for World-Action Models

items.title: Lost in Reconstruction: Aligning Action Representations with Language in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: This research explores how to align action representations with language in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, arguing that numerical proximity in raw action space does not adequately reflect how actions are performed.

items.title: JEPA-WAM: Stage-Level Joint-Embedding Prediction for World-Action Models in Robot Manipulation

items.title: Neural Introspection Gating for Adaptive KV-Cache Reuse in Vision-Language-Action Models

items.summary: Flex-pi is a multi-stream world-action model designed with compute flexibility, extending traditional WAMs to predict beyond RGB latents and incorporate 3D geometry or object semantics for improved future prediction.

items.summary: VIScore is a method for diagnosing the planning-relevant quality of latent world models, studying the connection between their latent space properties, such as isotropic Gaussian distribution, and successful planning outcomes.

items.title: From Cheap Fakes to Pure Synthesis: Addressing the New Era of T2V Fake News Videos
items.summary: This paper discusses the new threat of fake news videos synthesized entirely from scratch using advanced text-to-video generation models, highlighting the challenge for existing detection methods.

items.title: Capek 0.5: An Execution-Centric Vision-Language Model for Embodied Intelligence
items.summary: Capek 0.5 is presented as an execution-centric vision-language model serving as a reasoning core for embodied agents, specifically addressing the iterative nature of robot execution.

items.title: Surg-UniWorld: A Unified Surgical World Model with Multimodal Control Experts
items.summary: Surg-UniWorld introduces a unified surgical world model with multimodal control experts, providing a generative foundation for AI and simulation by synthesizing realistic instrument-tissue interactions.

items.title: ReGraph: Learning to Generate Recipe Graphs from Food Images
items.summary: ReGraph is a method for learning to generate structured recipe graphs from food images, extending the capabilities of large multimodal models in recipe generation beyond free-form text.

items.title: Stockmark-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-JapanDocReader: Structured Document Parsing via Capability Injection and Forgetting Control
items.summary: This paper introduces Stockmark-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-JapanDocReader, a new Japanese document understanding model built from Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16. Its goal is structured document parsing through capability injection and forgetting control.

items.title: PHASE-Tree: Modeling Character-State Evolution in Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue
items.summary: PHASE-Tree is a model designed to address character-state evolution in long-horizon role-playing dialogue, allowing characters to remain consistent while evolving with the narrative. It aims to improve upon static character profiles in AI-driven storytelling.

items.title: Stoicheia: Character-Level Masked Diffusion for Ancient Greek Textual Restoration, Parsing, and Metrical Scansion
items.summary: Stoicheia is a 405M-parameter character-level masked-diffusion encoder model designed for Ancient Greek textual restoration, parsing, and metrical scansion. It processes input across five independently maskable planes, including letters and linguistic features.

items.title: Multi Codec Discrete Diffusion Model for Text Guided Speech Inpainting and Editing
items.summary: This paper introduces a multi-codec discrete diffusion model specifically designed for text-guided speech inpainting and editing tasks. The model aims to reconstruct missing or corrupted speech segments and modify spoken content.

items.title: TransSLR: A Lightweight Transformer for Sign Language Recognition
items.summary: TransSLR introduces a lightweight Transformer model designed for automated Sign Language Recognition, particularly focusing on under-represented languages like Central African Sign Language to improve accuracy in this domain.

items.title: CoDAT: Collaborative Dual-Attention Transformer with Low-Cost Temporal Modeling for Efficient Edge Action Recognition
items.summary: This paper introduces CoDAT, a collaborative dual-attention transformer designed for low-cost temporal modeling, enabling efficient real-time human action recognition. The model is optimized for deployment on Internet-of-Things (IoT) edge devices with strict resource constraints.

items.title: WaveFreqAnchor: Wave-Structural Anchoring and Frequency Correction Diffusion for Training-Free Face Restoration
items.summary: This paper introduces WaveFreqAnchor, a training-free method for face restoration using diffusion models that employs wave-structural anchoring and frequency correction. It addresses issues of structural drift and degraded fidelity in existing diffusion-based face restoration under severe conditions.

items.title: Beyond Starry Night: Shortcut-Aware Control-State Planning for Artist-Grounded Text to Image Generation
items.summary: This research presents a method for 'shortcut-aware control-state planning' to improve artist-grounded text-to-image generation, moving beyond models' reliance on generic artist-specific shortcuts. The goal is to generate images that better preserve the user's intended scene and artistic style.

items.title: Explore or Converge? Stage-Guided Per-Step Optimization for Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper explores 'stage-guided per-step optimization' for diffusion models, utilizing reinforcement learning to align their generative capabilities with specific user preferences. The method aims to overcome the limitations of maximum likelihood training in achieving desired outcomes.

items.title: UniCycleFlow: Bidirectional Unpaired Image Translation with a Shared Rectified Flow
items.summary: This paper proposes UniCycleFlow, a new method for bidirectional unpaired image translation that utilizes a shared rectified flow to preserve source-specific structures. It aims to learn coherent transformations in both directions without requiring paired supervision, improving upon existing approaches.

items.title: PAST: Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination for Efficient Diffusion Model
items.summary: This paper introduces PAST (Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination), a method to improve the efficiency of diffusion models for text-to-image tasks. It aims to optimize downstream objectives and address the low efficiency of existing fine-tuning methods using reinforcement learning.

items.title: Bend the Basics: Degradation-Aware Deformable Tokenization for All-in-One Image Restoration
items.summary: This paper proposes 'Degradation-Aware Deformable Tokenization' for all-in-one image restoration, aiming to develop a single model capable of recovering images degraded by diverse corruptions. The method addresses limitations of fixed patch partitioning in unified Transformer models.

items.title: GOPI: Generation-Oriented 3D Pose Inference for Furniture Insertion from Single-View RGB-D Indoor Scenes
items.summary: This paper presents GOPI, a generation-oriented method for 3D pose inference, enabling the insertion of new furniture into indoor scene images from single-view RGB-D inputs. The approach addresses the challenge of physically grounded furniture placement when scale is underdetermined.

items.title: ControlRef: Efficient Layout-Guided Multi-Instance Generation via Anchored 4D-RoPE
items.summary: This paper proposes ControlRef, an efficient method for layout-guided multi-instance generation in Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) using anchored 4D-RoPE. It aims to improve controllable image synthesis by addressing challenges in integrating this capability into unified architectures.

items.title: HazeSpikeMamba: Coupling Spiking-Inspired and State-Space Features for Self-Supervised Real-World Dehazing
items.summary: This paper introduces HazeSpikeMamba, a novel model for self-supervised real-world dehazing that couples spiking-inspired and state-space features. The model addresses the performance drop of dehazing networks when applied to real photographs compared to synthetic data.

items.title: Prune Once: Retraining-Free Task-Agnostic Pruning for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces 'Prune Once,' a retraining-free and task-agnostic pruning method designed to reduce the computational and memory requirements of Vision-Language Models (VLMs). The technique aims to facilitate the deployment of VLMs in constrained environments by improving their efficiency.

items.title: MaskFlow: Precise, Consistent and Seamless Regional Image Editing
items.summary: MaskFlow is presented as a new method for precise, consistent, and seamless regional image editing, overcoming challenges in localized and natural edits despite strong semantic alignment.

items.title: AVCap: Reinforcing Audio-Video Joint Caption with Detail-Aware Reward
items.summary: AVCap proposes a new method for reinforcing audio-video joint captioning with detail-aware reward, essential for multimodal video understanding and generation, by addressing dataset scarcity and limitations of prior reinforcement learning.

items.title: HRDiT: Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation with Off-the-Shelf Diffusion Transformer Models
items.summary: HRDiT introduces a training-free method for high-resolution image generation by adapting off-the-shelf Diffusion Transformer models, extending capabilities beyond U-Net-based approaches.

items.title: InstanceSplat: Instance-Aware Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Scene Understanding
items.summary: This paper introduces InstanceSplat, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method for instance-aware 3D reconstruction and scene understanding, addressing limitations in existing category-oriented approaches.

items.title: Representation-driven Endoscopic Visual Embedding Alignment for Latent Generation
items.summary: This research explores representation alignment to improve the efficiency of developing foundation generative models, such as Diffusion Transformers, for endoscopic visual embedding and latent generation.

items.title: Flow-Corrected Shape Optimization: Taming Manifold Drift in High-Dimensional 3D Models
items.summary: This paper introduces Flow-Corrected Shape Optimization to address manifold drift, a critical failure mode encountered when optimizing 3D shapes within the latent spaces of deep generative models.

items.title: CANIS: Generation-Assisted 3D Canonicalization via an Image-Semantic Bridge
items.summary: CANIS is proposed as a category-agnostic, generation-assisted method for 3D object canonicalization, using an image-semantic bridge to achieve semantically meaningful orientations.

items.title: Is Forward Prediction Enough? Physical State Grounding for JEPA World Models
items.summary: This research investigates whether forward prediction is sufficient for JEPA-based world models, proposing physical state grounding to enhance their learning of structured and control-relevant latent representations.

items.title: Decoupling Intention from Trajectory: A Representational Deduction Framework for World Action Models
items.summary: This paper proposes a Representational Deduction Framework for World Action Models (WAMs) to decouple intention from trajectory, enhancing their ability to understand world state evolution and guide generative motion planning.

items.title: EffectLearner: World-Aware Object-Effect Reasoning for Real-World Video Object Removal

items.title: CoordRefer: Coordinate-Aware 3D Visual Grounding from Multiview Images
items.summary: CoordRefer is a coordinate-aware 3D visual grounding method from multiview images that predicts a coordinate frame and regresses a 3D bounding box for localization.

items.title: Dual-Output Multi-Exposure HDR Reconstruction via SDR Fusion and Gain Map Inverse Tone Mapping
items.summary: DOME-HDR is a dual-output multi-exposure HDR reconstruction framework that jointly produces a perceptually balanced SDR image and a consistent HDR image via gain map inverse tone mapping.

items.title: SCI-CLIP: Segment-Centric Inference with Reference Memory for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
items.summary: SCI-CLIP offers segment-centric inference with reference memory for training-free open-vocabulary segmentation, addressing limitations in patch-level vision-language features.

items.title: ChronoVision: Temporal Reasoning via Latent State Reconstruction
items.summary: ChronoVision improves temporal reasoning in multimodal large language models for complex visual cognitive tasks by using latent state reconstruction to articulate continuous visual changes.

items.title: Vorch-IR: Long-Form Unified Multimodal Identity Replacement Video Generation
items.summary: Vorch-IR is a method for long-form unified multimodal identity replacement video generation, capable of transferring identities while preserving motion, expressions, and temporal structure.

items.title: Vorch-Streamer: Extending Human Audio-Visual Generation to Real-Time Long-Form Streaming
items.summary: Vorch-Streamer extends human audio-visual generation to real-time long-form streaming, enabling causal, continuous synthesis with maintained audiovisual synchronization and visual consistency.

items.title: URNet: A Unified Reparameterized Network for Efficient RGB-D Semantic Segmentation

items.title: G$^2$ARD-GS: Geometry-Guided Anchor-Regularized Gaussian Splatting Distillation
items.summary: G$^2$ARD-GS is a geometry-guided anchor-regularized Gaussian Splatting distillation method designed to reduce the storage, transmission, and rendering costs of 3D Gaussian Splatting models.

items.title: PhyLatent: Learning Dynamics-Relevant Representations for JEPA World Models
items.summary: PhyLatent proposes a dynamics-relevant training objective for JointEmbedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models, aiming to preserve physical states and action consequences in representations.

items.title: Engram-E2VID: Reference-Based Event-to-Video Reconstruction via Generative Activation of Appearance Engrams
items.summary: This paper introduces Engram-E2VID, a method for reconstructing RGB video frames from an event stream and a reference frame by leveraging generative activation of appearance engrams. It aims to recover fine-grained temporal cues to create video from sparse event data.

items.title: LiteKD-Net: Lightweight Knowledge-Distilled Network for Mobile Image Denoising
items.summary: LiteKD-Net is a lightweight, knowledge-distilled network designed for mobile image denoising, focusing on achieving good restoration quality with low computational cost. It addresses the challenge of limited large-scale training data by using a physics-guided noise simulation.

items.title: ConceptADapt: Concept-guided Adaptive Feature Reconstruction with Dynamic Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection
items.summary: ConceptADapt is a method for few-shot industrial anomaly detection that uses concept-guided adaptive feature reconstruction with dynamic attention to identify visual defects. It is designed for scenarios with limited normal training samples per category.

items.title: UniVVT: A Unified End-to-End Framework for High-Fidelity Video Virtual Try-on
items.summary: UniVVT is a unified end-to-end framework designed for high-fidelity video virtual try-on, which synthesizes video of a person wearing a target garment while preserving identity, motion, and scene dynamics. It aims to integrate separate modules for a more coherent solution.

items.title: HyTBE: Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert Model for Cross-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection
items.summary: HyTBE is a Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert Model designed for cross-domain infrared small target detection, aiming to improve performance when generalizing to unseen infrared domains. It focuses on enhancing target responses and suppressing background noise.

items.title: Vorch-Director: Interactive World Story Model via Noise-Aware Error Rectification
items.summary: Vorch-Director is an interactive world story model that uses noise-aware error rectification for minute-scale audio-visual generation. It extends a short-window generator to produce continuous audio and video content.

items.title: Evidence-Driven Dynamic Visual Selector for Efficient Long Video Understanding
items.summary: This paper presents an Evidence-Driven Dynamic Visual Selector designed to improve efficient long video understanding for MLLM-based systems by selecting query-relevant frames. The approach aims to mitigate computational costs and context length limitations without relying on external proxy scorers.

items.title: VSMP-IMU: Video-Grounded Semantic Motion Programs for Sensor-Aware Synthetic IMU Generation
items.summary: VSMP-IMU introduces Video-Grounded Semantic Motion Programs for generating synthetic IMU data, aiming to reduce dependency on labeled sensor data for wearable human activity recognition. This method helps enhance HAR machine learning model performance, especially in low-resource settings.

items.title: KVAE: Family of Tokenizers for Multimodal Generative Models
items.summary: KVAE is a family of tokenizers designed for multimodal generative models, particularly within latent diffusion modeling, to map input signals to compressed representations. These tokenizers are integral to the generation process, impacting learning speed and quality of synthesized outputs.

items.title: Vorch-Omni: Multi-Task Orchestration of Sight and Sound
items.summary: Vorch-Omni is a model for multi-task orchestration of sight and sound, building on advances in generative video modeling. It aims to provide diverse generation, reference-based synthesis, extension, and editing capabilities by distinguishing various signal types.

items.title: Ordered Diffusion for 3D Human Registration
items.summary: Ordered Diffusion is a method for 3D human registration, addressing the inherent ambiguity in human scans caused by acquisition noise, occlusions, and soft tissue dynamics. It moves beyond traditional regression tasks to provide more robust alignment.

items.title: STAIL: Semantic Text-Anchored Incremental Learning for Medical Imaging via Large Language Models
items.summary: STAIL proposes Semantic Text-Anchored Incremental Learning for medical imaging, utilizing Large Language Models to mitigate catastrophic forgetting when continually adapting to new clinical tasks. This method moves beyond pixel-level rehearsal by leveraging semantic text anchors.

items.title: VLAff: Vision-Language-Affordance Model for Unified Actionable Affordances
items.summary: VLAff is a Vision-Language-Affordance Model designed to learn unified actionable affordances for robot manipulation skills from human videos. It aims to bridge the embodiment mismatch between humans and robots by focusing on object-centric, embodiment-agnostic affordances.

items.title: MMaDA-VLA: Large Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model with Unified Multi-Modal Instruction and Generation
items.summary: MMaDA-VLA is a large diffusion Vision-Language-Action model that offers unified multi-modal instruction and generation capabilities for mapping visual observations and natural language to robot actions.

items.title: DFM-VLA: Iterative Action Refinement for Robot Manipulation via Discrete Flow Matching
items.summary: DFM-VLA proposes an iterative action refinement method for robot manipulation using Vision-Language-Action models and discrete flow matching to improve action decoding.
